19:47: Imam Ahmad said: Abdul Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ibn Al-Musayyab, on the authority of his father, who said: When Abu Talib was about to die, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon him and Abu Jahl and Abdullah bin Abi Umayya were with him. He said, O uncle, say, 'There is no god but God,' a word by which I will argue for you before God Almighty. Abu Jahl and Abdullah bin Abi Umayya said, O Abu Talib, are you turning away from the religion of Abdul Muttalib? He said, I am on the religion of Abdul Muttalib. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, I will seek forgiveness for you as long as I am not forbidden from doing so. Then the verse was revealed, It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of Hellfire. He said, And the verse was revealed about him, 'Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but God guides whom He wills.' Bukhari and Muslim. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Adam told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Khalil, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: I heard a man asking forgiveness for his parents, even though they were polytheists. I said: Does a man ask forgiveness for his parents, even though they were polytheists? He said: Did not Ibrahim ask forgiveness for his father? I mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the verse was revealed: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for polytheists 1:13. He said: When he died, I do not know whether Sufyan said it, or Israel said it, or it is in the hadith when he died. I said: This is confirmed from Mujahid that he said when he died. Imam Ahmad said: Al-Hasan bin Musa told us, Zuhair told us, Zubayd bin Al-Harith Al-Yami told us, on the authority of Muharib bin Dithar, on the authority of Ibn Buraydah, on the authority of his father, who said: We were with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and we were on a journey. He stopped with us, and we were close to a thousand riders. He prayed two rak’ahs, then turned to us with his face and his eyes were shedding tears. Umar bin Al-Khattab stood up and said: O Messenger of God, what is the matter with you? He said, “I asked my Lord, the Almighty, to seek forgiveness for my mother, but He did not permit me, so my eyes welled up with tears out of mercy for her from the Fire. I had forbidden you from three things: I forbade you from visiting graves, so visit them, for visiting them will remind you of good. I forbade you from eating the meat of sacrifices after three days, so eat and hold back as much as you wish. I forbade you from drinking beverages in vessels, so drink from any vessel you wish, but do not drink intoxicants.” Ibn Jarir narrated from the hadith of Alqamah bin Murthad from Sulayman bin Buraydah from his father that when the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Makkah, he came to a grave and sat down next to it and began to address it, then he stood up weeping. We said, O Messenger of God, we have seen what you did. He said, “I asked my Lord for permission to visit my mother’s grave and He gave me permission. I asked Him for permission to seek forgiveness for her, but He did not give me permission.” He was never seen weeping more than that day. Ibn Abi Hatim said in his interpretation of the hadeeth: My father told us, Khalid bin Khidash told us, Abdullah bin Wahb told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ayoub bin Hani’, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) went out one day to the graveyards, so we followed him. He came and sat next to one of the graves, and he confided in it for a long time, then he wept, and we wept because of his weeping. Then he stood up and ‘Umar bin Al-Khattab stood up to him and called him, then he called us, and he said, What made you weep? We said, We wept because of your weeping. He said: The grave that I sat at is the grave of Amina, and I asked permission from my Lord to visit her, and He gave me permission. Then he mentioned it from another source, then he mentioned a hadith from Ibn Mas`ud similar to it, in which it says: “And I asked permission from my Lord to pray for her, but He did not give me permission, and He revealed to me, ‘It is not for the Prophet and those who believe,’ the verse, and I was seized by what a son seizes for his father, and I had forbidden you from visiting graves, so visit them, for they remind you of the Hereafter.” Another hadith with the same meaning. Al-Tabarani said: Muhammad bin Ali Al-Marwazi told us, Abu Al-Darda Abdul Aziz bin Munib told us, Ishaq bin Abdullah bin Kaysan told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned from the Battle of Tabuk and performed the minor pilgrimage, and when he descended from Thaniyat Usfan, he ordered his companions to lean on the pass until he returned to them. So he went and descended upon his mother’s grave and communed with his Lord for a long time, then he cried and his crying became intense and these people cried because of his crying, and they said, The Prophet of God did not cry in this place except because God had done something to his nation that they could not bear. So when these people cried, he stood up and returned to them and said, What makes you cry? They said, O Prophet of God, we cried because of your crying, and we said, perhaps something has happened in your nation that you cannot bear. He said, “No, and some of it happened, but I came down to my mother’s grave and asked God to allow me to intercede for her on the Day of Resurrection, but God refused to allow me, so I took pity on her, even though she was my mother, and I cried. Then Gabriel came to me and said, “And Abraham’s asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disassociated himself from him.” So you disassociate yourself from your mother as Abraham disassociated himself from his father. So I took pity on her, even though she was my mother, and I asked my Lord to lift four things from my nation, and He lifted two from them, but He refused to lift two. I asked my Lord to lift the stoning from the sky and the drowning from the earth, and not to confuse them into sects and not to let some of them taste the violence of others, so God lifted the stoning from the sky and the drowning from the earth, but God refused to lift the killing and chaos from them.” He only went to his mother’s grave because she was buried under Kada’ and it was Usfan. For them, this is a strange hadith and a strange context, and stranger than it and more reprehensible is what Al-Khatib Al-Baghdadi narrated in the book Al-Sabiq wa Al-Lahiq with an unknown chain of transmission on the authority of Aisha in a hadith that contains a story, that God revived his mother so she believed and then returned, and likewise what Al-Suhayli narrated in Al-Rawdh with a chain of transmission that contains a group of unknown al-Nas 114:God revived his father and mother so they believed in him. Al-Hafiz Ibn Dihya said about this evidence, the gist of which is that this is a new life just as the sun returned after its setting, so Ali prayed the afternoon prayer. Al-Tahawi said: It is an authentic hadith, meaning the hadith of the sun. Al-Qurtubi said: Their revival is not impossible rationally or religiously. He said: I heard that God revived his uncle Abu Talib so he believed in him. I said All of this depends on the authenticity of the hadith, so if it is authentic then there is nothing wrong with it, and God knows best. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists 3:10, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, wanted to ask forgiveness for his mother, but God Almighty forbade him from doing so. He said: Indeed, Abraham, the friend of God, has asked forgiveness for his father. So God revealed: And Abraham’s asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him 3:10. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding this verse: They used to ask forgiveness for them until this verse was revealed. So they refrained from asking forgiveness for their dead, and they were not forbidden from asking forgiveness for the living until they died. Then God revealed: And Abraham’s asking forgiveness for his father 3:10. Qatada said regarding the verse: It was mentioned to us that some men from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Prophet of God, some of our fathers were good neighbors, maintained family ties, freed the captives, and fulfilled their obligations. Should we not ask forgiveness for them? He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Yes, by God, I seek forgiveness for my father as Abraham sought forgiveness for his father. Then God revealed: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, until he reached the words Hellfire. Then God Almighty excused Abraham, peace be upon him, and said: And it was not for Abraham to ask forgiveness for his father, the verse. He said: And it was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “God revealed to me words that entered my ears and settled in my heart: I was commanded not to ask forgiveness for one who died a polytheist, and whoever gives his surplus wealth, it is better for him, and whoever withholds it, it is worse for him, and God does not blame anyone for what is sufficient.” Al-Thawri said, on the authority of Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: A Jewish man died and he had a Muslim son, but he did not go out with him. This was mentioned to Ibn Abbas, who said: He should have walked with him, buried him, and prayed for his well-being as long as he was alive. Then when he died, he left him to his own affairs. Then he said: “And Abraham’s seeking of forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disassociated himself from him.” He did not pray. And what testifies to its authenticity is what Abu Dawud and others narrated on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, that when Abu Talib died, I said, O Messenger of God, your uncle, the misguided old man, has died. He said, Go and bury him and do not say anything until you come to me. So he mentioned the entire hadith. And it was narrated that when the funeral of his uncle Abu Talib passed by him, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said, May mercy reach you, O uncle. And Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah said, “I would not neglect to pray for any of the people of the Qiblah, even if it were an Ethiopian woman who was pregnant from fornication, because I have not heard God prohibit prayer except for the polytheists. God Almighty says, “It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists.” Ibn Jarir narrated, on the authority of Ibn Wakee’, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Asma bin Zamil, on the authority of his father, who said: I heard Abu Hurairah say: May God have mercy on a man who seeks forgiveness for Abu Hurairah and his mother. I said: And for his father? He said: No. He said: My father died as a polytheist, and his statement: And when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disowned him. Ibn Abbas said: Ibrahim continued to seek forgiveness for his father until he died, and when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disowned him. In another narration: When he died, it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God. This is what Mujahid, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, and others, may God have mercy on them, said. Ubayd ibn Umair and Sa`id ibn Jubayr said: He will disown him on the Day of Resurrection until he meets his father, and on his father’s face is dust and dirt, and he will say: O Ibrahim, I used to disobey you, but today I do not disobey you. He will say: O Lord, did you not promise me that you would not disgrace me on the Day of Resurrection? What disgrace is greater than that of my distant father? It will be said: Look behind you, and there he is a hyena covered in blood, that is, he has been transformed into a hyena, then he will be dragged by his legs and thrown into the Fire. And his saying: Indeed, Abraham was most compassionate and forbearing. Sufyan al-Thawri and others said: On the authority of Asim ibn Bahdalah, on the authority of Zur ibn Hubaish, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Masoud, that he said: Awwa is supplication. And it was narrated in this way from more than one source: On the authority of Ibn Masoud, and Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna told me, Al-Hajjaj ibn Munhal told us, Abdul Hamid ibn Bahram told us, Shahr ibn Hawshab told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Haad, who said: While the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting, a man said: O Messenger of God, what is awwa? He said: The one who beseeches. He said: Indeed, Abraham was most compassionate and forbearing. And Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it: From the hadith of Ibn al-Mubarak, on the authority of Abdul Hamid ibn Bahram, with it, and its wording is: He said: The one who beseeches and beseeches and supplicates. And al-Thawri said, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhayl, on the authority of Muslim al-Batin, on the authority of Abu al-Ghadir, that he asked Ibn Masoud about awwa and he said: He is the Most Merciful. And Mujahid, Abu Maysarah, Umar ibn Shurahbil, al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatadah, and others said the same, meaning the Most Merciful, meaning to the servants of God. Ibn Al-Mubarak said on the authority of Khalid on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Al-Awah is the one who is certain in the language of Abyssinia. Al-Awfi said the same on the authority of Ibn Abbas that it is al-Muwakeen. Mujahid and Ad-Dahhak said the same. Ali bin Abi Talhah and Mujahid said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Al-Awah is the believer. Ali bin Abi Talhah added on his authority: He is the repentant believer. Al-Awfi said on his authority that it is the believer in the language of Abyssinia. Ibn Jurayj said the same that it is the believer in the language of Abyssinia. Imam Ahmad said: Musa told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Al-Harith bin Yazid, on the authority of Ali bin Rabah, on the authority of Uqbah bin Amir, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to a man called Dhu Al-Bijadayn, He is the one who glorifies God. That is because he was a man who, when God was mentioned in the Qur’an, would raise his voice in supplication. It was narrated by Ibn Jarir. Saeed bin Jubair and Al-Sha’bi said, The one who glorifies God is the one who praises God. Ibn Wahb said, on the authority of Mu’awiyah bin Salih, on the authority of Abu Al-Zahariyyah, on the authority of Jubayr bin Nufayr, on the authority of Abu Al-Darda’, may God be pleased with him, who said, No one maintains the Duha prayer bead except the one who glorifies God. Shafi bin Mani’ said, on the authority of Abu Ayoub, The one who glorifies God is the one who, when he remembers his sins, seeks forgiveness for them. It was narrated by Mujahid, on the authority of the one who glorifies God, who secretly commits a sin and then secretly repents from it. All of this was mentioned by Ibn Abi Hatim, may God have mercy on him. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Wakee’ told us, Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Muslim bin Bayan, that a man used to frequently mention God and glorify God, so he mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said, He is the one who glorifies God. He also said: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, Ibn Hani’ narrated to us, Al-Munhal bin Khalifa narrated to us, on the authority of Hajjaj bin Artah, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, buried a dead person and said: May God have mercy on you, for you were indeed a recitation of the Qur’an. Shu’bah narrated on the authority of Abu Yunus Al-Bahili, who said: I heard a man in Mecca who was originally Roman and was a storyteller, narrating on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: There was a man who used to circumambulate the Sacred House and say in his supplication: Oh, oh. So he mentioned that to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: He is indeed a recitation of the Qur’an. He said: So I went out one night and saw the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, burying that man at night with a lamp. This is a strange hadith narrated by Ibn Jarir. It was narrated on the authority of Ka’b Al-Ahbar that he said: I heard Indeed, Ibrahim was indeed a recitation of the Qur’an. He said: Whenever the Fire was mentioned, he would say: Oh, from the Fire. Ibn Jurayj said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Indeed, Ibrahim was indeed a recitation of the Qur’an. He said: A jurist. Imam Abu Jaafar bin Jarir said: The most correct of the sayings is the saying of the one who said that it is a supplication, and it is appropriate for the context, and that is because when God Almighty mentioned that Abraham only asked forgiveness for his father for a promise he had made to him, and Abraham was a frequent supplicant and forbearing towards those who wronged him and caused him harm, and for this reason he asked forgiveness for his father despite his severe harm to him in his saying: Are you averse to my gods, O Abraham? If you do not desist, I will stone you, and leave me for a long time. He said, “Peace be upon you! I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, He is ever Gracious to me.” So he was forbearing towards him despite his harm to him, and he supplicated for him and asked forgiveness, and for this reason God Almighty said: Indeed, Abraham was most kind and forbearing. God the Almighty says, informing about the answer of Abraham's father to his son Abraham in what he called him to, that he said: Do you reject my gods, O Abraham? Meaning, if you do not want to worship them and are not pleased with them, then stop cursing, insulting and criticizing them, because if you do not stop, I will take revenge on you, insult you and curse you, and this is His saying: I will stone you, said by Ibn Abbas, As-Suddi, Ibn Jurayj, Ad-Dahhak and others. And His saying: And leave me for a long time, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr and Muhammad bin Ishaq said: It means for a long time. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: A long time. As-Suddi said: And leave me for a long time, he said: Forever. Ali bin Abi Talha and Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And leave me alone for a long time, meaning: in good health and safety before I punish you. This is what Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Atiyah Al-Jadali, Malik and others said, and Ibn Jarir chose it. So when Ibrahim said to his father, “Peace be upon you,” as God Almighty said in describing the believers: “And when the ignorant address them, they say, ‘Peace. ’” And God Almighty said: “And when they hear ill speech, they turn away from it and say, ‘To us our deeds, and to you your deeds. Peace be upon you. We seek not the ignorant. ’” The meaning of Ibrahim’s saying to his father, “Peace be upon you,” means as for me, no harm or injury will come to you from me, due to the sanctity of fatherhood. I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord, but I will ask God for you to guide you and forgive your sin. Indeed, He has been ever gracious to me. Ibn Abbas and others said: Kind, meaning in that He guided me to worship Him and be sincere to Him. Qatada, Mujahid and others said: He was kind to me. He said, He returned the answer. Al-Suddi said: The one who is concerned about his affairs, and Abraham, peace be upon him, sought forgiveness for his father for a long time after he migrated to the Levant, and built the Sacred Mosque, and after he had Ishmael and Isaac, peace be upon them, in his saying: Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the Day the account is established. And the Muslims sought forgiveness for their relatives and families from the polytheists at the beginning of Islam, and this was following the example of Abraham, the friend of God, in that until God Almighty revealed: “There has certainly been for you an excellent pattern in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, ‘Indeed, we are disassociated from you and from whatever you worship other than God. We have rejected you, and there has arisen between us and you animosity and hatred forever until you believe in God alone.’” Except for the saying of Abraham to his father, I will surely ask forgiveness for you, but I do not possess for you anything against God. The verse, meaning except in this saying, so do not follow his example, then God Almighty explained that Abraham stopped doing that and returned from it, so God Almighty said: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of Hellfire. And Abraham's seeking of forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him. But when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disassociated himself from him. Indeed, Abraham was most kind and forbearing. And His statement: And I will leave you and those you invoke besides God and invoke my Lord. That is, I will worship my Lord alone, with no partner for Him. Perhaps I will not be, in invoking my Lord, unhappy. And this perhaps is inevitable, for he, peace be upon him, is the master of the prophets after Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.
19:1: Surah Maryam It is Meccan Muhammad bin Ishaq narrated in the biography from the hadith of Umm Salamah, and Ahmad bin Hanbal from Ibn Masoud in the story of the migration to the land of Abyssinia from Mecca that Jaafar bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, recited the beginning of this surah to the Negus and his companions. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful As for the discussion of the disconnected letters, it was mentioned at the beginning of Surat Al-Baqarah. His saying, mention the mercy of your Lord, means that this is a mention of God’s mercy to His servant Zachariah. Yahya bin Ya’mar read, mention the mercy of your Lord to His servant Zachariah, and Zachariah is lengthened and shortened. These are two well-known readings. He was a great prophet from the prophets of the Children of Israel. In Sahih Al-Bukhari, it is mentioned that he was a carpenter who ate from the work of his hand in carpentry. And his saying, When he called upon his Lord, a secret call, some of the commentators said: He only concealed his supplication so that he would not be accused of being reckless in his request for a child due to his old age. Al-Mawardi narrated it. Others said: He only concealed it because it was dearer to God, as Qatada said about this verse, When he called upon his Lord, a secret call, that God knows the pious heart and hears the secret voice. Some of the predecessors said: He, peace be upon him, got up at night and his companions were asleep, so he began to call out to his Lord, saying secretly: O Lord, O Lord, O Lord, so God said to him: At your service, at your service, at your service. He said, O Lord, indeed my bones have grown feeble, meaning I have become weak and my strength has failed, and my head is ablaze with gray hair, meaning the gray hair has burned into the blackness, as Ibn Duraid said in his book, Al-Maqsura: Don't you see that my head is the color of a morning's forehead under the covers of darkness? The ovary caught fire in a draft like the burning of embers of the ghada tree. What is meant by this is to inform about weakness and arrogance and their apparent and hidden signs. And his saying, And I have never been unhappy in my supplication to You, my Lord, means, I have never known from You anything but an answer to my supplication, and You have never turned me away from what I asked of You. And his saying, And I feared my relatives after me, most of them read the ya’ of mawali in the accusative case as if it were a direct object. According to Al-Kisa’i, he made the ya’ sukoon, as the poet said: As if their hands in the bottom of the tinkling floor were the hands of maids dealing paper The other said: A young man who, if he could compete with the sun, would throw off its mask, or the moon, would throw off its necklace. And from it is the saying of Abu Tammam Habib bin Aws al-Ta’i: His poetry was so different that I stayed up all night to recite it, I thought his rhymes would fight. Mujahid, Qatada and As-Suddi said: By mawali he meant the agnates. Abu Salih said: Kalalah. It was narrated on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman ibn Affan, may God be pleased with him, that he used to recite it, And indeed, I feared my agnates after me, with a shaddah on the fa, meaning I said, My agnates after me. According to the first reading, the reason for his fear was that he feared that they would treat people badly after him, so he asked God for a son who would be a prophet after him to govern them with his prophethood as He revealed to him. He was answered in that, not that he feared that they would inherit his money, for a prophet is of a greater status and greater rank than to fear for his money to this extent, or to be disgusted by his agnates’ inheritance of him, and to ask to have a son so that he could take his inheritance without them. This is one reason. Second It was not mentioned that he had money, but rather that he was a carpenter who ate from the earnings of his hands, and such a person does not accumulate money, especially the prophets, for they were the most ascetic in this world. Third It has been proven in the two Sahihs from more than one source that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, We do not inherit, what we leave behind is charity. And in a narration by al-Tirmidhi with a sound chain of transmission, We, the community of prophets, do not inherit. Based on this, it is necessary to interpret his statement, Then grant me from Yourself an heir who will inherit me, as referring to the inheritance of prophethood. For this reason, he said, And he inherits from the family of Jacob, like his statement, And Solomon inherited from David, meaning in prophethood, because if it had been in wealth, he would not have singled him out from among his brothers for that, and there would not have been much benefit in informing about that, since it is well-known and established in all laws and religions that the son inherits from his father. If it were not a special inheritance, he would not have informed about it. All of this is confirmed and proven by what is authentic in the hadith, We, the community of prophets, do not inherit, what we leave behind is charity. Mujahid said about his statement, He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob, his inheritance was knowledge, and Zakariya was from the descendants of Jacob. Hisham said: Ismail bin Abi Khalid informed us on the authority of Abu Salih on his statement, He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob, he said: He will be a prophet as his fathers were prophets. Abd al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of al-Hasan, he will inherit his prophethood and his knowledge. Al-Suddi said: He will inherit my prophethood and the prophethood of the family of Jacob. Malik on the authority of Zaid bin Aslam, And he will inherit from the family of Jacob, he said: Their prophethood. Jabir bin Nuh and Yazid bin Harun both said on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih on his statement, He will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob, he said: He will inherit my money and inherit the prophethood from the family of Jacob. This is the choice of Ibn Jarir in his interpretation. Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Qatada that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: May God have mercy on Zachariah and what he had to do with inheriting his wealth, and may God have mercy on Lot, for he used to take refuge in a strong support. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Jabir bin Nuh told us on the authority of Mubarak, who is Ibn Fadala, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God have mercy on my brother Zachariah and what he had to do with inheriting his wealth when he said: ‘Grant me from Yourself an heir who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Jacob.’” These are mursal hadiths that do not contradict the sahih hadiths, and God knows best. His statement, And make him, my Lord, pleasing means pleasing to You and to Your creation, You love him and make him beloved to Your creation in his religion and his character.

This is evidence that Zakariya, peace be upon him, did not have children, and likewise his wife was barren from the beginning of her life, unlike Abraham and Sarah, peace be upon them, for they were only amazed at the good report of Isaac because of their old age, not because of their barrenness. For this reason he said: “You have given me good report, although old age has touched me. So with what good report do you give me?” even though he had given birth to Ishmael thirteen years before him, and his wife said: Woe to me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman and my husband an old man? Indeed, this is a strange thing. They said: “Do you wonder at the command of God? The mercy of God and His blessings be upon you, O people of the House. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Glorious.”

He was extremely happy and asked about how he would be born and the way in which the son would come to him, even though his wife was barren and had not given birth since the beginning of her life despite her old age, and even though he had grown old and emaciated, meaning his bones had become thin and there was no longer any sperm or intercourse in him. Ibn Abbas and others said: `atyan means old age, and it appears that it is more specific than old age. Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub told us, Hisham told us, Hisin told us on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I have learned the entire Sunnah, except that I do not know whether the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite in the noon and afternoon prayers or not, and I do not know how he used to recite this letter: And you have reached a ripe old age or in the deepest depths. Easy means simple and easy for God. Then He mentioned to him something more amazing than what he asked about, so He said: And I created you before, and you were nothing, as God the Almighty said: Has there not been over man a period of time when he was not a thing worth mentioning?

19:10: God the Almighty says, informing us about Zachariah, peace be upon him, that he said, My Lord, make for me a sign, meaning a sign and evidence of the existence of what you promised me, so that my soul may be at ease and my heart may be reassured by what you promised me, as Abraham, peace be upon him, said, My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead. He said, Do you not believe? He said, Yes, but so that my heart may be at ease. The verse, He said, 'Your sign,' meaning your mark, 'is that you will not speak to the people for three nights without illness or defect.' That is, that you will keep your tongue from speaking for three nights, while you are healthy and sound, without illness or defect. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Wahb, As-Suddi, Qatadah, and others said: His tongue was held back without illness or defect. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: He used to recite and glorify God, but he was not able to speak to his people except by gestures. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Three consecutive nights, meaning consecutive. The first statement on his authority and on that of the majority is more correct, as God Almighty said in Al-Imran, “He said, ‘My Lord, make for me a sign.’ He said, ‘Your sign is that you will not speak to the people for three days except by gesture. This is evidence that he did not speak to the people during these three nights and days, except by gesture, meaning by a sign. That is why He said in this noble verse, Then he came out to his people from the sanctuary, meaning the one in which he gave the good report of the son. And he inspired them, meaning he gestured quickly, to glorify Him morning and evening, meaning in agreement with what he was commanded to do during these three days, in addition to his deeds, in gratitude to God for what He had given him. Al-Suddi said the same.

19:12: This also included an omission, the estimation of which is that he found this boy who was promised, and he is John, peace be upon him, and that God taught him the Book, which is the Torah that they studied among themselves, and the prophets who submitted to the Jews, the rabbis and the scholars ruled by it, and he was young at that time, so he mentioned him and what he bestowed upon him and his parents, so he said: O John, take the Book with strength, meaning learn the Book with strength, meaning with diligence, eagerness and effort, and We gave him judgment while he was a boy, meaning understanding, knowledge, diligence, resolve, turning to goodness and devoting oneself to it and striving for it while he was a young boy. Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak said: Muammar said: The boys said to John bin Zakariya: Go with us and let us play, so he said: You were not created for play, so for this reason God revealed and We gave him judgment while he was a boy. And His statement: And compassion from Us Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And compassion from Us means: And mercy from Us. And this is what Ikrimah, Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak said, and he added: None but Us can do it. And Qatadah added: May God have mercy on Zachariah with it. And Mujahid said: And compassion from Us and compassion from his Lord towards him. And Ikrimah said: And compassion from Us he said: Love for him. And Ibn Zayd said: As for compassion, it is love. And Ata bin Abi Rabah said: And compassion from Us he said: Exaltation from Us. And Ibn Jurayj said: Amr bin Dinar told me that he heard Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: No, by God, I do not know what compassion is. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Jarir told us on the authority of Mansur, I asked Saeed bin Jubair about his statement: And compassion from Us, he said: I asked Ibn Abbas about it and he did not find anything in it. It appears from the context that his statement And compassion is connected to his statement: And We gave him wisdom while he was a boy, meaning We gave him wisdom, compassion, and purity, meaning We made him possessor of compassion and purity. So compassion is love with compassion and inclination, as the Arabs say: The she-camel yearned for her young, and the woman yearned for her husband, and from this the woman was called Hannah from henna, and the man yearned for his homeland, and from this comes compassion and mercy, as the poet said: Have mercy on that king, for every situation has its own words. In Al-Musnad of Imam Ahmad, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “A man will remain in Hell calling out for a thousand years: ‘O Most Compassionate, O Most Generous.’” It may be dual, and some of them consider what was mentioned in this to be a language in itself, as Tarafa said: Abu Munther, you have perished, so let some of us outlast your kindness. Some evil is less serious than others. His statement: and purity is connected to tenderness, so purity is the purity from filth, sins and transgressions. Qatada said: Zakat is righteous deeds. Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Jurayj said: The righteous, pure deed. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: and purity he said: blessing, and he was God-fearing he was pure and did not intend to sin. Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: “A person is most lonely in three situations: the day he is born and sees himself emerging from what he was in; the day he dies and sees a people he has never seen; and the day he is resurrected and sees himself in a great gathering place.” He said: “So God honored Yahya ibn Zakariya in it and singled him out with peace, saying: ‘Peace be upon him the day he was born, the day he dies, and the day he is resurrected alive.’” Narrated by Ibn Jarir on the authority of Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Marwazi on the authority of Sadaqah ibn al-Fadl on his authority. Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: a tyrant, disobedient, he said: Ibn Al-Musayyab used to mention that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No one will meet God on the Day of Resurrection except with a sin, except for Yahya bin Zakariya. Qatada said: He did not sin nor did he intend to have intercourse with a woman, mursal. Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, Ibn Al-Aas told me that he heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “Every son of Adam will come on the Day of Resurrection and he will have a sin, except for Yahya bin Zakariya bin Ishaq. Saeed bin Abi Arubah said on the authority of Qatada that Al-Hasan said: Yahya and Jesus, peace be upon them, met, and Jesus said to him: Ask forgiveness for me, you are better than me, so the other said to him: Ask forgiveness for me, you are better than me, so Jesus said to him: You are better than me, you greeted myself, and God greeted you, so God recognized their superiority.

This is extremely strange and unusual, and it seems as if it were an Israelite. She said, ‘Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you should be fearing God.’ That is, when the angel appeared to her in the form of a human being while she was in a separate place and there was a veil between her and her people, she feared him and thought that he wanted to harm her, so she said: Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you should be fearing God, meaning if you fear God, reminding him of God. This is the prescribed way of warding off evil, which is to do what is easiest and then what is easiest. So she frightened him. First of all, by God Almighty. So her Lord accepted her with good acceptance and caused her to grow in a good manner. She grew up among the Children of Israel in a great manner, and was one of the pious and ascetic women known for her great worship, devotion, and diligence. 19:22: The Almighty says, informing about Mary, that when Gabriel told her about God Almighty what he said, she submitted to the decree of God Almighty. More than one of the scholars of the Salaf mentioned that the angel, who was Gabriel, peace be upon him, then blew into the pocket of her garment, and the blow descended until it entered her vagina, and she became pregnant with the child, with the permission of God Almighty. When she became pregnant with him, she was fed up, and did not know what to say to the people, for she knew that the people would not believe her in what she told them. However, she divulged her secret and mentioned her matter to her sister, the wife of Zachariah. That was because Zachariah, peace be upon him, had asked God for a child, and he was granted that, so his wife became pregnant. Mary entered upon her, and she stood up to her and embraced her and said: Do you know, O Mary, that I am pregnant? Mary said to her: Did you also know that I am pregnant? I mentioned to her her situation and what happened to her. They were a house of faith and belief. Then, after that, whenever Zachariah’s wife faced Mary, she would find the one in her womb prostrating to the one in Mary’s womb, meaning that he would glorify him and submit to him. For prostration was prescribed in their religion when greeting, just as Joseph’s parents and brothers prostrated to him, and just as God commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam, peace be upon him. However, it was forbidden in our religion to complete the glorification of the glory of the Almighty Lord. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn told us: It was read to al-Harith ibn Maskeen while I was listening. He said: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim told us: Malik, may God have mercy on him, said: It has reached me that Jesus, son of Mary, and John, son of Zakariya, peace be upon them, were cousins, and they were both conceived together. It has reached me that John’s mother said to Maryam 19:I see that what is in my womb prostrates to what is in your womb. Malik said: I see that because of the superiority of Jesus, peace be upon him, because God made him bring the dead back to life and heal the blind and the lepers. Then the commentators differed about the duration of Jesus’ pregnancy, peace be upon him. The well-known opinion of the majority is that she carried him for nine months. Ikrimah said: Eight months. He said: This is why a child born after eight months does not live. Ibn Jurayj said: Al-Mughira bin Uthman bin Abdullah Al-Thaqafi informed me that he heard Ibn Abbas when he was asked about Mary’s pregnancy. He said: It was not until she became pregnant and gave birth. This is strange, and it seems that it was taken from the apparent meaning of the Almighty’s statement: “So she conceived him and withdrew with him to a remote place. Then the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree.” So even though the fa is for subsequent confirmation, the confirmation of each thing is according to its nature, like the Almighty’s statement: “And We have certainly created man from an extract of clay. Then We placed him as a sperm-drop in a firm lodging. Then We made the sperm-drop into a clot, and We made the clot into a lump of flesh, and We made the lump of flesh into bones.” So this fa is for subsequent confirmation according to its nature. It has been proven in the two Sahihs that there are forty days between every two descriptions. God the Almighty said: Have you not seen that God sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green? So the well-known and apparent meaning is - and God is over all things competent - that she became pregnant with him as women become pregnant with their children. For this reason, when the signs of pregnancy appeared on her, and there was with her in the mosque a righteous man from her relatives who served with her in the Holy House, his name was Joseph the Carpenter. When he saw the heaviness and size of her belly, he was dismayed by that, then he was distracted by what he knew of her innocence, purity, religion and worship. Then he pondered what she was in, so her matter began to run through his mind and he was unable to distract it from himself. He forced himself to present it to her in speech, so he said: O Mary, I am going to ask you about a matter, so do not be hasty with me. She said: What is it? He said: Can there ever be a tree without a seed? And can there be a plant without a seed? And can there be a child without a father? She said: Yes, and she understood what he was referring to. As for your saying: Can there be a tree without a seed and a plant without a seed? God created the tree and the plant without a seed when He first created them. And can there be a child without a father? God Almighty created Adam without a father or a mother, so He believed her and accepted her situation. And when Mary sensed that her people were accusing her of suspicion, she withdrew from them to a distant place, that is, far from them, so that she would not see them and they would not see her. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: When she became pregnant with him and filled her womb and returned, the blood stopped flowing from her and she was afflicted with what a pregnant woman feels for a child, such as pain, cravings, and a change in color, until her tongue was broken. No household was affected by what the family of Zachariah experienced. The story spread among the Children of Israel and they said: Only Joseph accompanied her and there was no one with her in the church except him. She hid from the people and took a veil from them, so no one could see her and she could not see him. His statement: Then the labor pains drove her to the trunk of the palm tree means that the labor pains forced her and compelled her to the trunk of the palm tree in the place where she carved out. They differed about it. Al-Suddi said: It was to the east of her prayer niche in which she prayed in the Holy House. Wahb bin Munabbih said: She went fleeing, and when she was between Syria and Egypt, labor pains struck her. And in a narration on the authority of Wahb: That was eight miles from Jerusalem in a village there called Bethlehem. I said: It was mentioned in the hadiths of the Night Journey from the narration of al-Nasa’i on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, and al-Bayhaqi on the authority of Shaddad ibn Aws, may God be pleased with him, that that was in Bethlehem. And God knows best. And this is the well-known view that people have received from one another, and the Christians have no doubt that it was in Bethlehem, and the people have received it, and the hadith has been transmitted with it if it is authentic. God the Almighty said, informing about her: She said, ‘Oh, I wish I had died before this and been in oblivion and forgotten.’ This is evidence of the permissibility of wishing for death at times of trial, for she knew that she would be tested and tried with this child, about whom people would not believe her story, and after she had been a pious worshipper among them, she would become, in their view, a prostitute and adulterer. So she said: Oh, I wish I had died before this, meaning before this state, and been in oblivion and forgotten, meaning I had not been created and I was nothing, as Ibn Abbas said. Al-Suddi said, while she was being released from the rope, out of shyness from the al-Nas 114:Oh, I wish I had died before this distress that I am in and the grief of giving birth to a child without a husband, “and was in oblivion and forgotten, forgotten and abandoned, like menstrual rags that when they are thrown away and discarded are not sought and are not remembered. Likewise, everything that is forgotten and abandoned is forgotten. Qatada said: And was in oblivion and forgotten, meaning something that is not known or remembered and does not know who I am. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: And I was forgotten and forgotten meaning the miscarriage. Ibn Zayd said: I was never anything. We have already presented the hadiths indicating the prohibition of wishing for death except in times of trial, when he said: Let me die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous.

Mary entered upon her, and she stood up to her and embraced her and said: Do you know, O Mary, that I am pregnant? Mary said to her: Did you also know that I am pregnant? I mentioned to her her situation and what happened to her. They were a house of faith and belief. Then, after that, whenever Zachariah’s wife faced Mary, she would find the one in her womb prostrating to the one in Mary’s womb, meaning that he would glorify him and submit to him. For prostration was prescribed in their religion when greeting, just as Joseph’s parents and brothers prostrated to him, and just as God commanded the angels to prostrate to Adam, peace be upon him. However, it was forbidden in our religion to complete the glorification of the glory of the Almighty Lord. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn told us: It was read to al-Harith ibn Maskeen while I was listening. He said: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim told us: Malik, may God have mercy on him, said: It has reached me that Jesus, son of Mary, and John, son of Zakariya, peace be upon them, were cousins, and they were both conceived together. It has reached me that John’s mother said to Maryam 19:I see that what is in my womb prostrates to what is in your womb. Malik said: I see that because of the superiority of Jesus, peace be upon him, because God made him bring the dead back to life and heal the blind and the lepers. Then the commentators differed about the duration of Jesus’ pregnancy, peace be upon him. The well-known opinion of the majority is that she carried him for nine months. Ikrimah said: Eight months. He said: This is why a child born after eight months does not live. Ibn Jurayj said: Al-Mughira bin Uthman bin Abdullah Al-Thaqafi informed me that he heard Ibn Abbas when he was asked about Mary’s pregnancy. He said: It was not until she became pregnant and gave birth. This is strange, and it seems that it was taken from the apparent meaning of the Almighty’s statement: “So she conceived him and withdrew with him to a remote place. Then the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree.” So even though the fa is for subsequent confirmation, the confirmation of each thing is according to its nature, like the Almighty’s statement: “And We have certainly created man from an extract of clay. Then We placed him as a sperm-drop in a firm lodging. Then We made the sperm-drop into a clot, and We made the clot into a lump of flesh, and We made the lump of flesh into bones.” So this fa is for subsequent confirmation according to its nature. It has been proven in the two Sahihs that there are forty days between every two descriptions. God the Almighty said: Have you not seen that God sends down water from the sky, and the earth becomes green? So the well-known and apparent meaning is - and God is over all things competent - that she became pregnant with him as women become pregnant with their children. For this reason, when the signs of pregnancy appeared on her, and there was with her in the mosque a righteous man from her relatives who served with her in the Holy House, his name was Joseph the Carpenter. When he saw the heaviness and size of her belly, he was dismayed by that, then he was distracted by what he knew of her innocence, purity, religion and worship. Then he pondered what she was in, so her matter began to run through his mind and he was unable to distract it from himself. He forced himself to present it to her in speech, so he said: O Mary, I am going to ask you about a matter, so do not be hasty with me. She said: What is it? He said: Can there ever be a tree without a seed? And can there be a plant without a seed? And can there be a child without a father? She said: Yes, and she understood what he was referring to. As for your saying: Can there be a tree without a seed and a plant without a seed? God created the tree and the plant without a seed when He first created them. And can there be a child without a father? God Almighty created Adam without a father or a mother, so He believed her and accepted her situation. And when Mary sensed that her people were accusing her of suspicion, she withdrew from them to a distant place, that is, far from them, so that she would not see them and they would not see her. Muhammad bin Ishaq said: When she became pregnant with him and filled her womb and returned, the blood stopped flowing from her and she was afflicted with what a pregnant woman feels for a child, such as pain, cravings, and a change in color, until her tongue was broken. No household was affected by what the family of Zachariah experienced. The story spread among the Children of Israel and they said: Only Joseph accompanied her and there was no one with her in the church except him. She hid from the people and took a veil from them, so no one could see her and she could not see him. His statement: Then the labor pains drove her to the trunk of the palm tree means that the labor pains forced her and compelled her to the trunk of the palm tree in the place where she carved out. They differed about it. Al-Suddi said: It was to the east of her prayer niche in which she prayed in the Holy House. Wahb bin Munabbih said: She went fleeing, and when she was between Syria and Egypt, labor pains struck her. And in a narration on the authority of Wahb: That was eight miles from Jerusalem in a village there called Bethlehem. I said: It was mentioned in the hadiths of the Night Journey from the narration of al-Nasa’i on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, and al-Bayhaqi on the authority of Shaddad ibn Aws, may God be pleased with him, that that was in Bethlehem. And God knows best. And this is the well-known view that people have received from one another, and the Christians have no doubt that it was in Bethlehem, and the people have received it, and the hadith has been transmitted with it if it is authentic. God the Almighty said, informing about her: She said, ‘Oh, I wish I had died before this and been in oblivion and forgotten.’ This is evidence of the permissibility of wishing for death at times of trial, for she knew that she would be tested and tried with this child, about whom people would not believe her story, and after she had been a pious worshipper among them, she would become, in their view, a prostitute and adulterer. So she said: Oh, I wish I had died before this, meaning before this state, and been in oblivion and forgotten, meaning I had not been created and I was nothing, as Ibn Abbas said. Al-Suddi said, while she was being released from the rope, out of shyness from the al-Nas 114:Oh, I wish I had died before this distress that I am in and the grief of giving birth to a child without a husband, “and was in oblivion and forgotten, forgotten and abandoned, like menstrual rags that when they are thrown away and discarded are not sought and are not remembered. Likewise, everything that is forgotten and abandoned is forgotten. Qatada said: And was in oblivion and forgotten, meaning something that is not known or remembered and does not know who I am. Al-Rabi’ bin Anas said: And I was forgotten and forgotten meaning the miscarriage. Ibn Zayd said: I was never anything. We have already presented the hadiths indicating the prohibition of wishing for death except in times of trial, when he said: Let me die as a Muslim and join me with the righteous.
19:24: Some of them read: from beneath her meaning the one beneath her, and others read: from beneath her as a preposition, and the commentators differed about who is meant by that? Al-Awfi and others said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: So he called to her from beneath her means Gabriel, and Jesus did not speak until she brought him to her people. And this is what Saeed bin Jubair, Al-Dahhak, Amr bin Maymun, Al-Suddi and Qatadah said: It is the angel Gabriel, peace be upon him, meaning he called to her from the bottom of the valley. And Mujahid said: So he called to her from beneath her means Jesus, son of Mary. And this is what Abd Al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatadah who said: Al-Hasan said: He is her son, and this is one of the two narrations on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair that he is her son. He said: Did you not hear God say: So she pointed to him and this was chosen by Ibn Zayd and Ibn Jarir in their interpretation. And his saying: Do not grieve means he called to her saying do not grieve. Your Lord has provided a stream beneath you. Sufyan al-Thawri and Shu’bah said on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib Your Lord has provided a stream beneath you he said: the brook. And Ali ibn Abi Talhah said the same on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas: the brook is the stream, and ‘Amr ibn Maymun said the same as the river from which you drink. And Mujahid said: it is the river in Syriac. And Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: the brook is the small river in Nabataean. And al-Dahhak said: it is the small river in Syriac. And Ibrahim al-Nakha’i said: it is the small river. And Qatada said: it is the brook in the language of the people of Hijaz. And Wahb ibn Munabbih said: the brook is the spring water. And al-Suddi said: it is the river, and Ibn Jarir chose this statement. A hadith with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) was narrated on this subject. At-Tabarani said: Abu Shu’ayb al-Harrani narrated to us, Yahya ibn ‘Abdullah al-Babli narrated to us, Ayoub ibn Nahik narrated to us, I heard ‘Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn ‘Abbas, say, I heard Ibn ‘Umar say: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: The secret that God said to Maryam, ‘Your Lord has provided beneath you a stream’ is a river that God brought forth for her to drink from. This hadeeth is very strange from this perspective. This Ayoub ibn Nahik is the pregnant woman. Abu Hatim al-Razi said about him: He is weak. Abu Zur’ah said: He is a denier of hadeeth. Abu al-Fath al-Azdi said: He is a rejected hadeeth. Others said that what is meant by the secret is Jesus, peace be upon him. This is what al-Hasan, al-Rabi’ ibn Anas, and Muhammad ibn ‘Ibad ibn Ja’far said, and it is one of the two narrations from Qatada, and the statement of ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and the first statement is more apparent. This is why he said after it: And shake the trunk of the palm tree towards you, meaning, take the trunk of the palm tree towards you. It was said: It was dry, as Ibn ‘Abbas said. It was also said: It was fruitful. Mujahid said: It was Ajwa dates. Ath-Thawri said on the authority of Abu Dawud Nafi’ al-Ama: It was Sarfana, and it appears that it was a tree, but it was not in its fruiting season, as Wahb ibn Munabbih said. That is why He bestowed upon her a favor by making food and drink available to her, saying: “It will drop upon you ripe, fresh dates. So eat and drink and be refreshed.” That is, be content. That is why Amr ibn Maymun said: There is nothing better for a woman in childbirth than dates and fresh dates. Then he recited this noble verse. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Shaiban told us, Masrur bin Saeed Al-Tamimi told us, Abdul Rahman bin Amr Al-Awza’i told us on the authority of Urwah bin Ruwaim on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Honor your paternal aunt, the palm tree, for it was created from the same clay from which Adam, peace be upon him, was created, and there is no tree that pollinates other than it.” The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Feed your women fresh dates, and if there are no fresh dates, then dried dates, and there is no tree more honorable to God than the tree under which Mary, daughter of Imran, descended. This is a very strange hadith and Abu Ya’la narrated it on the authority of Shaiban. Some of them read tasaqat with a shaddah on the seen, and others with a light seen. Abu Nahik read tataqat alaykum tantuban yanya. Abu Ishaq narrated on the authority of Al-Bara’ that he read it as tasaqat meaning the trunk, and all are similar. And his saying: So if you see anyone from among mankind meaning, no matter what you see of anyone, say, ‘Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast, so I will not speak to any human being today.’ What is meant by this saying is to indicate that, not that what is meant by it is the verbal statement so that it does not contradict I will not speak to any human being today. Anas bin Malik said about his saying: Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful a fast, he said: Silence. Ibn Abbas and Ad-Dahhak said the same. In a narration from Anas: Fasting and silence. Qatada and others said the same. What is meant is that when they fasted, according to their religion, food and speech were forbidden to them. As-Suddi, Qatada, and Abd ar-Rahman bin Zaid stated this explicitly. Abu Ishaq said on the authority of Haritha, who said: I was with Ibn Masoud, and two men came, one of them greeted the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) but the other did not. He said: What is the matter with you? His companions said: He swore that he would not speak to people today. Abdullah bin Masoud said: Speak to people and greet them, for that is a woman who knows that no one will believe her that she became pregnant without a husband, meaning Mary, peace be upon her, so that it will be an excuse for her if she is asked. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on them. Abdul Rahman bin Zaid said: When Jesus said to Maryam 19:Do not grieve, she said: How can I not grieve when you are with me, neither a husband nor a slave? What excuse do I have before people? I wish I had died before this and been forgotten. Jesus said to her: I will suffice you in speaking. “But if you see any human being, say: ‘Indeed, I have vowed to the Most Merciful to fast, so I will not speak to any human being today.’” All of this was from Jesus’ speech to his mother, and Wahb said the same.

19:27: God the Almighty says, informing us about Mary when she was ordered to fast that day and not to speak to any human being, for her matter would be taken care of and her argument would be established. She submitted to the command of God the Almighty and surrendered to His judgment. She took her son and brought him to her people, carrying him. When they saw her like that, they greatly appreciated her matter and found it very strange. “They said, ‘O Mary, you have certainly done a thing unprecedented. ’” That is, a great matter. This was said by Mujahid, Qatadah, As-Suddi, and others. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad told us, Sayyar told us, Ja’far bin Sulayman told us, Abu Imran Al-Jawni told us on the authority of Nawf Al-Bakali, who said: Her people went out in search of her. He said: She was from a family of prophethood and honor, but they did not sense anything in her. They met a cowherd and said: Did you see such-and-such a girl? Describe her. He said: No, but tonight I saw from my cows what I had never seen from them before. They said: What did you see? He said: I saw her tonight prostrating towards this valley. Abdullah bin Ziyad said: I remember from Sayyar that he said: I saw a bright light, so they headed where he told them to, and Mary met them, and when she saw them, she sat down and carried her son in her lap, so they came until they stood over her. They said: O Mary, you have certainly done a thing unprecedented, a great matter, O sister of Aaron, meaning O one who resembles Aaron in worship, Your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste, meaning you are from a good, pure family known for righteousness, worship, and asceticism, so how did this come from you? Ali bin Abi Talhah and Al-Suddi said: It was said to her: O sister of Aaron, meaning brother of Moses, and she was from his lineage, just as a Tamimi is called: O brother of Tamim, and a Mudari is called: O brother of Mudar. He said: She was from a family of prophethood and honor, but they did not sense anything in her. They met a cowherd and said: Did you see such-and-such a girl? Describe her. He said: No, but tonight I saw from my cows what I had never seen from them before. They said: What did you see? He said: I saw her tonight prostrating towards this valley. Abdullah bin Ziyad said: I remember from Sayyar that he said: I saw a bright light, so they headed where he told them to, and Mary met them, and when she saw them, she sat down and carried her son in her lap, so they came until they stood over her. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad told us, Sayyar told us, Ja’far bin Sulayman told us, Abu Imran Al-Jawni told us on the authority of Nawf Al-Bakali, who said: Her people went out in search of her. He said: She was from a family of prophethood and honor, but they did not sense anything in her. They met a cowherd and said: Did you see such-and-such a girl? Describe her. He said: No, but tonight I saw from my cows what I had never seen from them before. They said: What did you see? He said: I saw her tonight prostrating towards this valley. Abdullah bin Ziyad said: I remember from Sayyar that he said: I saw a bright light, so they headed where he told them to, and Mary met them, and when she saw them, she sat down and carried her son in her lap, so they came until they stood over her. They said: O Mary, you have certainly done a thing unprecedented, a great matter, O sister of Aaron, meaning O one who resembles Aaron in worship, Your father was not a man of evil, nor was your mother unchaste, meaning you are from a good, pure family known for righteousness, worship, and asceticism, so how did this come from you? Ali bin Abi Talhah and Al-Suddi said: It was said to her: O sister of Aaron, meaning brother of Moses, and she was from his lineage, just as a Tamimi is called: O brother of Tamim, and a Mudari is called: O brother of Mudar. It was said: She was attributed to a righteous man among them whose name was Aaron, so she was compared to him in asceticism and worship. Ibn Jarir narrated from some of them that they likened her to a wicked man among them whose name was Aaron. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, and stranger than all of this is what Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Ali bin Al-Hussein Al-Hijistani narrated to us, Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Al-Mufaddal bin Fadala narrated to us, Abu Sakhr narrated to us on the authority of Al-Qurazi regarding the words of God Almighty: O sister of Aaron, he said: She is the sister of Aaron from his father and mother, and she is the sister of Moses, the brother of Aaron, who followed the traces of Moses, and she saw him from a distance while they did not perceive. This statement is a complete error, for God Almighty mentioned in His Book that He followed Jesus after the messengers, which indicates that he was the last of the prophets to be sent, and after him there is no one but Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon them both. For this reason, it was proven in Sahih Al-Bukhari on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, that he said: I am the closest of people to the son of Mary, except that there is no prophet between me and him. If the matter was as Muhammad bin Ka’b Al-Qurazi claimed, then no one came after the messengers except Muhammad, and he would have been before Solomon and David, for God Almighty mentioned that David came after Moses. Peace be upon them in the words of God Almighty: Have you not considered the assembly of the Children of Israel after Moses, when they said to a prophet of theirs, ‘Send us a king, and we will fight in the way of God,’ and he mentioned the story until he said: And David killed Goliath, the verse, and what made Al-Qurazi dare to say this is what is in the Torah after Moses and the Children of Israel came out of the sea and Pharaoh and his people were drowned, he said: And Mary, the daughter of Imran, the sister of the prophets Moses and Aaron, was beating the tambourine with the women with her, praising God and thanking Him for what He had bestowed upon the Children of Israel, so Al-Qurazi believed that this was the mother of Jesus, and this was a grave mistake and error, rather she was named after this one, and they used to name themselves after the names of their prophets and righteous people, as Imam Ahmad said: Abdullah bin Idris told us, I heard my father mention it on the authority of Samak on the authority of Alqamah bin Wa’il on the authority of Al-Mughirah bin Shu’bah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me to Najran, and they said: What do you think of what you read, O sister of Aaron, and Moses was before Jesus by such and such? He said: So I went back and mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said: Did you not tell them that they used to name themselves after the prophets and righteous people before them? Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa’i alone transmitted it from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Idris, from his father, from Samak, and al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan sahih gharib, we do not know it except from the hadith of Ibn Idris. Ibn Jarir said: Ya’qub told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us, from Sa’id ibn Abi Sadaqa, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: I was informed that Ka’b said that his saying, O sister of Aaron, does not refer to Aaron, the brother of Moses. Aisha said to him: You have lied. He said: O Mother of the Believers, if the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said it, then he is more knowledgeable and informed, otherwise I find that there were six hundred years between them. So she remained silent. There is some doubt about this date. Ibn Jarir also said: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: O sister of Aaron the verse, he said: She was from a family known for their righteousness and not for their corruption, and among the people there are those who are known for their righteousness and they procreate through it, and others are known for their corruption and they procreate through it, and Aaron was a beloved reformer among his clan, and he was not Aaron, the brother of Moses, but another Aaron. He said: And it was mentioned to us that forty thousand people accompanied his funeral procession on the day he died, all of them called Aaron from the Children of Israel. And His saying: “So she pointed to him. They said: How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?” That is, when they were suspicious of her matter and disapproved of her case and said to her what they said, in an attempt to slander and accuse her of lying, and she was fasting and silent that day, so she referred the matter to him and pointed to his speech and words, so they said mockingly, thinking that she was disdaining them and playing with them, How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child? Maymun ibn Mihran said: So she pointed to him she said speak to him, so they said: With what she has brought of calamity, you command us to speak to one who is in the cradle, and Al-Suddi said that when she pointed to him they became angry and said: Her mockery of us until she commands us to speak to this child is more severe for us than her fornication. “They said: How can we speak to one who is in the cradle, a child?” That is, one who is in his cradle in his childhood and youth, how does he speak? He said: I am the servant of God. The first thing he said was to declare his Lord Almighty free from having a son, and to affirm for himself the servitude of his Lord. And his saying: He has given me the Book and made me a prophet is an exoneration of his mother from the immorality attributed to him. Nawf al-Bakali said: When they said to his mother what they said, he was suckling his breast, so he took the breast from his mouth and leaned on his left side and said: “Indeed, I am the servant of God. He has given me the Book and made me a prophet. And He has made me blessed wherever I may be. And He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakat as long as I live.” Hammad ibn Salamah said on the authority of Thabit al-Banani: He raised his index finger above his shoulder while saying: “Indeed, I am the servant of God. He has given me the Book and made me a prophet.” The verse. Ikrimah said: He has given me the Book means that He decreed that He would give me the Book in what He decreed. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Muhammad ibn al-Musaffa told us, Yahya ibn Saeed - he is al-Attar - told us on the authority of Abd al-Aziz ibn Ziyad, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, may God be pleased with him, who said: Jesus, son of Mary, had studied the Torah and mastered it while he was in his mother’s womb, so that is what he said: “Indeed, I am the servant of God. He has given me the Book.” And made me a prophet. Yahya bin Saeed Al-Attar Al-Himsi is rejected. And His statement: And He has made me blessed wherever I may be. Mujahid, Amr ibn Qays and Ath-Thawri said: And He has made me a teacher of goodness. And in a narration from Mujahid: Beneficial. Ibn Jarir said: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me, Muhammad ibn Yazid ibn Khunais al-Makhzumi told us, I heard Wahib ibn al-Ward, a client of Banu Makhzum, say: A scholar met another scholar who was above him in knowledge, and he said to him: May God have mercy on you, what is my action that I have declared? He said: Enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, for it is the religion of God with which He sent His prophets to His servants. The jurists have agreed upon the statement of God: And He has made me blessed wherever I may be. And it was said: What is its blessing? He said: Enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong wherever it may be. And His statement: And He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakat as long as I live is like the statement of God the Almighty to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty. Abdul Rahman bin Al-Qasim said on the authority of Malik bin Anas regarding his statement, And He enjoined upon me prayer and zakat as long as I live, he said: He informed him of what would happen to him until he died, how clear it is to the people of destiny. His saying: And dutiful to my mother means that He commanded me to be dutiful to my mother. He mentioned it after obeying God, his Lord, because God, the Most High, often links the command to worship Him with obeying parents, as He, the Most High, said: And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and to parents, good treatment (al-Baqarah 2:170) and He said: “Be grateful to Me and to your parents. To Me is the final destination.” His saying: And He has not made me a wretched tyrant means that He has not made me a wretched tyrant who refuses to worship Him, obey Him, and be dutiful to my mother, so that I would be wretched because of that. Sufyan al-Thawri said: The wretched tyrant is the one who kills in anger. Some of the early Muslims said: You will not find anyone disobedient to his parents except that you will find him a wretched tyrant. Then he recited: “And dutiful to my mother. And He has not made me a wretched tyrant” (al-Baqarah 2:170) He said: And you will not find anyone who is ill-mannered except that you will find him arrogant and proud. Then he recited: “And those whom your right hands possess. Indeed, God does not like anyone who is arrogant and boastful.” Qatada said: It was mentioned to us that a woman saw the son of Mary raising the dead and healing the blind and the leper in signs that God had given him authority over them and permitted him to do. She said: Blessed is the womb that bore you, and blessed is the breast that nursed you. The Prophet of God, Jesus, peace be upon him, said in response to her: Blessed is he who recites the Book of God and follows what is in it, and is not a wretched tyrant. His saying: “And peace be upon me the day I was born and the day I die and the day I am raised alive” is proof from him of his servitude to God, the Almighty, and that he is a creation of God’s creation who lives, dies, and is raised like all other creatures. However, he is safe in these conditions, which are the most difficult for the servants. May the prayers and peace of God be upon him.
