19:34: God Almighty says to His Messenger Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him: “That which We have related to you of the story of Jesus, peace be upon him, is the word of truth about which they are in doubt.” That is, the falsifiers and the truthful differ from those who believed in him and disbelieved in him. For this reason, the majority read the word of truth with the nominative case of saying. Asim and Abdullah bin Amir read the word of truth. Ibn Masoud said that he read it as Jesus, son of Mary. He said: The truth. The nominative case is more evident in grammar. This is supported by God Almighty’s statement: The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters. When God Almighty mentioned that He created him as a servant and prophet, He exalted His holy self and said: “It is not for God to take a son. Glory be to Him,” that is, above what these ignorant, unjust, and aggressive people say, When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, ‘Be,’ and it is. That is, when He wills something, He only commands it and it becomes as He wills, as He said: “Indeed, the likeness of Jesus before God is as that of Adam. He created him from dust and then said to him, ‘Be,’ and he was. The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.” And His statement: “And indeed, God is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.” That is, among what Jesus commanded his people to do while he was in his cradle was to inform them at that time that God was his Lord and their Lord, and he commanded them to worship Him, so he said: “So worship Him. This is a straight path.” That is, what I have brought to you from God is a straight path, that is, straight. Whoever follows it will be guided and will be guided, and whoever opposes it will go astray and go astray. And His statement: Then the parties differed among themselves. That is, the statements of the People of the Book differed regarding Jesus after his matter was made clear and his condition was made clear, and that he was His servant and His Messenger, and His word that He bestowed upon Mary and a spirit from Him. So a group of them, and they were the majority of the Jews - may God’s curses be upon them - insisted that he was born of fornication, and they said: His speech is magic. And another group said: God has spoken. And others said: Rather, he is the son of God. And still others said: The third of three. Others said: Rather, he is the servant and messenger of God, and this is the statement of truth to which God has guided the believers. Something similar to this has been narrated on the authority of Amr ibn Maymun, Ibn Jurayj, Qatadah, and more than one of the early and later generations. Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement: That is Jesus, the son of Mary - the word of truth about which they are in doubt. He said: The Children of Israel gathered and brought out four men from among them. Each group brought out their scholar. They doubted about Jesus when he was raised. Some of them said: He is God. He descended to earth and gave life to whom He gave life and caused death to whom He caused death. Then he ascended to heaven. They were the Jacobites. The three said: You have lied. Then two of them said to the third: You say about him. He said: He is the son of God. They were the Nestorians. The two said: You have lied. Then one of the two said to the other: Say about him. He said: He is the third of three: God is God, and he is God, and his mother is God. They were the Israelites, the kings of the Christians, upon them be the curses of God. The fourth said: You have lied. Rather, he is the servant of God and His Messenger, His Spirit and His Word. They were the Muslims. Each man among them had followers for what they said, so they fought and prevailed over the Muslims. This is what God Almighty said: And they kill those who enjoin justice among the people. Qatada said: They are the ones about whom God said: Then the parties differed among themselves. He said: They differed about it and became parties. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, and on the authority of some scholars, something similar to that. More than one of the historians from the People of the Book and others mentioned that Constantine gathered them in a large gathering of their three famous councils, and the group of bishops among them was two thousand one hundred and seventy bishops. They differed greatly about Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him. Each group said something about him, so one hundred said something about him, seventy said something else about him, fifty said something else, and one hundred and sixty said something. No more than three hundred agreed on one statement, and eight of them agreed on a statement and insisted on it. The king leaned towards them, and he was a philosopher, so he brought them forward and supported them and expelled those who opposed them. They placed for him the great trust, rather it is the great betrayal, and they placed for him books of laws and legislated things for him, and they innovated many innovations, and they distorted and changed the religion of Christ. So he built for them at that time the great churches in his entire kingdom, the lands of the Levant, the Peninsula, and Rome. The number of churches in his days was approximately Twelve thousand churches, and his mother Helena built a shrine on the place where the crucified one was crucified, whom the Jews and Christians claim is the Christ, but they lied, and God raised him to heaven. And His saying, So woe to those who disbelieve from the scene of a tremendous Day, is a severe threat and warning to those who lied about God, fabricated, and claimed that He has a son. However, God, the Almighty, will grant them respite until the Day of Resurrection, and He will grant them patience and trust in His power over them, for He is the One who does not hasten the punishment of those who disobey Him, as it came in the two Sahihs, Indeed, God grants respite to the wrongdoer until, when He seizes him, He does not let him escape. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited, “And such is the punishment of your Lord when He seizes the towns while they are wrongdoers. Indeed, His punishment is painful and severe.” And in the two Sahihs also, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said, “No one is more patient with the harm he hears than God. Indeed, they attribute to Him a son, while He provides for them and cures them.” And God, the Almighty, said, And how many a town was I granted respite while it was wrongdoing? Then I seized it, and to Me is the final destination. And God, the Almighty, said, “And never think that God is unaware of what the wrongdoers do. About what they were warned about on the Day of Regret and Remorse, and they do not believe, meaning they do not believe in it. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ubayd told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of Hell enter Hell, death will be brought like a white ram and will be made to stand between Paradise and Hell. O people of Hell, eternity and no death.’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited: ‘And warn them of the Day of Regret when the matter will be decided while they are in heedlessness and they will not believe.’ He pointed with his hand and said: ‘The people of this world are in the heedlessness of this world.’” This is how Imam Ahmad narrated it. Al-Bukhari and Muslim included it in their Sahihs from the hadith of Al-A’mash, and their wording is similar to that. This hadith was narrated by Al-Hasan bin Arafa: Asbat bin Muhammad told me, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, similarly. In Sunan Ibn Majah and others, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, something similar to it. It is in the two Sahihs, on the authority of Ibn Umar. Narrated by Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said, and those before him mentioned something similar. He also narrated it on the authority of his father that he heard Ubayd ibn Umair say in his al-Qasas 28:Death is brought as if it were a beast and is slaughtered while the people are watching. Sufyan al-Thawri said on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhail: Abu al-Zura’ told us on the authority of Abdullah - he is Ibn Mas’ud - in a story he mentioned, he said: There is no soul except that it looks at a house in Paradise and a house in Hell, and it is the Day of Regret. The people of Hell will see the house in Paradise, and it will be said to them, If only you had worked, so regret will overtake them. He said: And the people of Paradise will see the house in Hell, and it will be said to them, If only God had not been gracious to you. Al-Suddi said on the authority of Ziyad on the authority of Zur ibn Hubaysh on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud regarding his statement: And warn them of the Day of Regret when the matter is decided, he said: When the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of Hell enter Hell, death will be brought in the form of a white ram until it is stopped between Paradise and Hell. Then a caller will call out: O people of Paradise, this is the death that used to kill people in this world, so no one will remain in the highest place of Paradise or in the lowest level of Hell except that it will look at it. Then a caller will call out: O people of Hell, this is the death that used to kill people in this world, so no one will remain in the shallows of Hell or in the lowest level of Hell except that it will look at it. Then it will be slaughtered between Paradise and Hell. Then a call will be called out: O people of Paradise, this is eternity forever and ever, and O people of Hell, this is eternity forever and ever. So the people of Paradise will rejoice with a joy that if anyone were dead they would die from that joy, and the people of Hell will gasp with a gasp that if anyone were dead they would die from that gasp. That is what the Almighty said: And warn them of the Day of Regret when the matter is decided, meaning when death is slaughtered. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim in Its interpretation. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And warn them of the Day of Regret is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. God has made it great and warned His servants about it. Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said regarding his statement: And warn them of the Day of Regret he said: The Day of Resurrection, and he recited: That a soul will say, ‘Oh, how I regret what I neglected in my duty to God.’ And his statement: Indeed, it is We who inherit the earth and whoever is on it, and to Us they will be returned, God the Almighty informs us that He is the Creator, the Owner, the Disposer of affairs, and that all creation will perish and He, the Almighty and Holy, will remain, and no one claims ownership or control, rather He is the Inheritor of all His creation, the One who remains after them, the Ruler over them, so no soul will be wronged in the least, not even the wing of a mosquito or the weight of an atom. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Hadbah bin Khalid Al-Qaysi mentioned, Hazm bin Abi Hazm Al-Qat’i told us, he said: Umar bin Abdul Aziz wrote to Abdul Hamid bin Abdul Rahman, the ruler of Kufa: As for what follows, God decreed death for His creation when He created them, and He made their destiny to Him, and He said in what He revealed in His truthful book which He created with His knowledge and called His angels to witness to its preservation: He inherits the earth and whoever is on it, and to Him they will return.

In Sunan Ibn Majah and others, on the authority of Muhammad bin Amr, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, something similar to it. It is in the two Sahihs, on the authority of Ibn Umar. Narrated by Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said, and those before him mentioned something similar. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: And warn them of the Day of Regret is one of the names of the Day of Resurrection. God has made it great and warned His servants about it. Abd al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said regarding his statement: And warn them of the Day of Regret he said: The Day of Resurrection, and he recited: That a soul will say, ‘Oh, how I regret what I neglected in my duty to God.’ And his statement: Indeed, it is We who inherit the earth and whoever is on it, and to Us they will be returned, God the Almighty informs us that He is the Creator, the Owner, the Disposer of affairs, and that all creation will perish and He, the Almighty and Holy, will remain, and no one claims ownership or control, rather He is the Inheritor of all His creation, the One who remains after them, the Ruler over them, so no soul will be wronged in the least, not even the wing of a mosquito or the weight of an atom. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Hadbah bin Khalid Al-Qaysi mentioned, Hazm bin Abi Hazm Al-Qat’i told us, he said: Umar bin Abdul Aziz wrote to Abdul Hamid bin Abdul Rahman, the ruler of Kufa: As for what follows, God decreed death for His creation when He created them, and He made their destiny to Him, and He said in what He revealed in His truthful book which He created with His knowledge and called His angels to witness to its preservation: He inherits the earth and whoever is on it, and to Him they will return.

19:41: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And mention in the Book Abraham. And recite to your people who worship idols, and mention to them what happened with Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful. Those who are from his descendants and claim that they follow his religion, and he was a friend and prophet with his father, how did he forbid him from worshipping idols, and he said: O my father, why do you worship that which neither hears nor sees nor avails you at all? That is, it does not benefit you nor ward off harm from you? O my father, indeed there has come to me of knowledge that which has not come to you. He says: Even if I am from your lineage and you see me younger than you because I am your son, then know that I have been informed of knowledge from God that which you do not know, nor have you been informed of, nor has it come to you. So follow me, I will guide you to a straight path, that is, a straight path leading to attaining what is desired and salvation from what is feared. O my father, do not worship Satan, that is, do not obey him in your worship of these idols, for he is the one who calls to that and is pleased with it, as God Almighty said: Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you not worship Satan - indeed, he is to you a clear enemy? And He said: They invoke not besides Him except female deities, and they invoke not except a rebellious devil. And His statement, Indeed, Satan has been disobedient to the Most Merciful, meaning, disobedient and arrogant in obeying his Lord, so He expelled him and kept him far away, so do not follow him and persist like him. O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will afflict you, meaning, because of your polytheism and disobedience to what I command you. So you will be a friend of Satan, meaning, you will have no protector, helper, or supporter except Satan, and neither he nor anyone else has any authority over the matter. Rather, following him is a reason for the punishment to surround you, as God Almighty said, By God, We sent to nations before you, but Satan made their deeds pleasing to them, so he is their friend this Day, and for them is a painful punishment.

19:46: God the Almighty says, informing about the answer of Abraham's father to his son Abraham in what he called him to, that he said: Do you reject my gods, O Abraham? Meaning, if you do not want to worship them and are not pleased with them, then stop cursing, insulting and criticizing them, because if you do not stop, I will take revenge on you, insult you and curse you, and this is His saying: I will stone you, said by Ibn Abbas, As-Suddi, Ibn Jurayj, Ad-Dahhak and others. And His saying: And leave me for a long time, Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr and Muhammad bin Ishaq said: It means for a long time. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: A long time. As-Suddi said: And leave me for a long time, he said: Forever. Ali bin Abi Talha and Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And leave me alone for a long time, meaning: in good health and safety before I punish you. This is what Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Atiyah Al-Jadali, Malik and others said, and Ibn Jarir chose it. So when Ibrahim said to his father, “Peace be upon you,” as God Almighty said in describing the believers: “And when the ignorant address them, they say, ‘Peace. ’” And God Almighty said: “And when they hear ill speech, they turn away from it and say, ‘To us our deeds, and to you your deeds. Peace be upon you. We seek not the ignorant. ’” The meaning of Ibrahim’s saying to his father, “Peace be upon you,” means as for me, no harm or injury will come to you from me, due to the sanctity of fatherhood. I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord, but I will ask God for you to guide you and forgive your sin. Indeed, He has been ever gracious to me. Ibn Abbas and others said: Kind, meaning in that He guided me to worship Him and be sincere to Him. Qatada, Mujahid and others said: He was kind to me. He said, He returned the answer. Al-Suddi said: The one who is concerned about his affairs, and Abraham, peace be upon him, sought forgiveness for his father for a long time after he migrated to the Levant, and built the Sacred Mosque, and after he had Ishmael and Isaac, peace be upon them, in his saying: Our Lord, forgive me and my parents and the believers on the Day the account is established. And the Muslims sought forgiveness for their relatives and families from the polytheists at the beginning of Islam, and this was following the example of Abraham, the friend of God, in that until God Almighty revealed: “There has certainly been for you an excellent pattern in Abraham and those with him, when they said to their people, ‘Indeed, we are disassociated from you and from whatever you worship other than God. We have rejected you, and there has arisen between us and you animosity and hatred forever until you believe in God alone.’” Except for the saying of Abraham to his father, I will surely ask forgiveness for you, but I do not possess for you anything against God. The verse, meaning except in this saying, so do not follow his example, then God Almighty explained that Abraham stopped doing that and returned from it, so God Almighty said: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of Hellfire. Indeed, Abraham was most kind and forbearing. And His statement: And I will leave you and those you invoke besides God and invoke my Lord. That is, I will worship my Lord alone, with no partner for Him. Perhaps I will not be, in invoking my Lord, unhappy. And this perhaps is inevitable, for he, peace be upon him, is the master of the prophets after Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace.

19:49: God Almighty says: So when Abraham separated from his father and his people for the sake of God, God replaced him with someone better than them, and gave him Isaac and Jacob, meaning his son and the son of Isaac, as He said in the other verse: And Jacob as an additional son and He said: And after Isaac, Jacob. There is no dispute that Isaac was the father of Jacob, and this is the text of the Qur’an in Surat al-Baqarah 2:“Or were you witnesses when death approached Jacob, when he said to his sons, ‘What will you worship after me?’ They said, ‘We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac.’” That is why He only mentioned Isaac and Jacob here, that is, We made for him a progeny and descendants who were prophets with whom God pleased His eyes during his lifetime. That is why He said: And each of them We made a prophet. So if Jacob, peace be upon him, had not been a prophet during the lifetime of Abraham, He would not have limited himself to him and would have mentioned his son Joseph, for he is also a prophet, as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in the hadith whose authenticity is agreed upon when he was asked about the best of people, and he said: Joseph, the Prophet of God, the son of Jacob. The Prophet of God, son of Isaac, the Prophet of God, son of Abraham, the friend of God. In another version: The generous one, son of the generous one, son of the generous one, son of the generous one, Joseph, son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham. Al-Suddi and Malik ibn Anas said the same. Ibn Jarir said: He only said Ali because all religions and faiths praise and commend them, may the prayers and peace of God be upon them all.
19:50: God Almighty says: So when Abraham separated from his father and his people for the sake of God, God replaced him with someone better than them, and gave him Isaac and Jacob, meaning his son and the son of Isaac, as He said in the other verse: And Jacob as an additional son and He said: And after Isaac, Jacob. There is no dispute that Isaac was the father of Jacob, and this is the text of the Qur’an in Surat al-Baqarah 2:“Or were you witnesses when death approached Jacob, when he said to his sons, ‘What will you worship after me?’ They said, ‘We will worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham, Ishmael, and Isaac.’” That is why He only mentioned Isaac and Jacob here, that is, We made for him a progeny and descendants who were prophets with whom God pleased His eyes during his lifetime. That is why He said: And each of them We made a prophet. So if Jacob, peace be upon him, had not been a prophet during the lifetime of Abraham, He would not have limited himself to him and would have mentioned his son Joseph, for he is also a prophet, as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said in the hadith whose authenticity is agreed upon when he was asked about the best of people, and he said: Joseph, the Prophet of God, the son of Jacob. 19:51: When God mentioned Abraham, the friend of God, and praised him, He followed up by mentioning the one who spoke to God, saying: “And mention in the Book Moses. Indeed, he was sincere.” Some of them read it with a kasra on the lam from sincerity in worship. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Rafi’, on the authority of Abu Lubaba, who said: The disciples said: O Spirit of God, tell us about the one who is sincere to God? He said: The one who works for God does not like people to praise him. The others read it with a fatha, meaning that he was chosen, as God the Almighty said: Indeed, I have chosen you over mankind. “And he was a messenger and a prophet.” God combined for him the two descriptions, for he was one of the great messengers of strong resolve, and they are: Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus, and Muhammad, may the peace and blessings of God be upon them and upon all the other prophets. And His statement: And We called to him from the side of the Mount meaning the mountain to the right of Moses when he went in search of a live coal from that fire and saw it flashing, so he went towards it and found it on the right side of the Mount at the bank of the valley, so God Almighty spoke to him and called to him and brought him close and spoke to him privately. Ibn Jarir narrated: Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya - he is Al-Qattan - told us, Sufyan told us on the authority of Ata’ bin Al-Sa’ib, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We brought him close for a private conversation he said: He brought him close until he heard the scratching of the pen, and this is what Mujahid, Abu Al-Aaliyah and others said: they mean the scratching of the pen writing the Torah. Al-Suddi said: And We brought him close for a private conversation he said: He entered the sky and spoke, and Mujahid said something similar. Abdul Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, And We brought him near for a private conversation. He said: He was saved by his truthfulness. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Abdul-Jabbar bin Asim told us, Muhammad bin Salamah Al-Harrani told us, on the authority of Abu Wasil, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Amr bin Ma’dikarib, who said: When God brought Moses close to Him in secret at Mount Sinai, He said: O Moses, if I have created for you a grateful heart, a remembering tongue, and a wife who helps in goodness, then I will not withhold any goodness from you, and whoever I withhold this from, then I will not open for him any goodness. And His statement: And We bestowed upon him out of Our mercy his brother Aaron, a prophet means that We answered his question and his intercession for his brother, so We made him a prophet, as He said in the other verse: “And my brother Aaron is more eloquent than I in speech, so send him with me as a support to confirm me. Indeed, I fear that they will deny me.” And He said: Your request has been granted, O Moses. And He said: So send for Aaron * And they have a sin against me, so I fear that they will kill. 19:54: This is praise from God Almighty for Ismail bin Ibrahim Al-Khalil, peace be upon them, and he is the father of all the Arabs of Hijaz, that he was true to his promise. Ibn Jurayj said: He never made a promise to his Lord except that he fulfilled it, meaning that he never committed himself to worship with a vow except that he fulfilled it and fulfilled its right. Ibn Jarir said: Yunus told me, Ibn Wahb told us, Amr bin Al-Harith told me that Sahl bin Aqil told him that the Prophet Ismail, peace be upon him, promised a man a place to come to him, so he came and the man forgot, so Ismail stayed there and spent the night until the man came the next day, so he said: Did you not leave here? He said: No. He said: I forgot. He said: I would not leave until you came to me, so he was true to his promise. Sufyan Ath-Thawri said: It has reached me that he stayed in that place waiting for him for a year until he came to him. Ibn Shawdhab said: It has reached me that he made that place a residence. Abu Dawud narrated in his Sunan, and Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Ja`far al-Kharaiti in his book Makarim al-Akhlaq, on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Tahman, on the authority of Badil ibn Maysarah, on the authority of `Abd al-Karim, meaning ibn `Abdullah ibn Shaqiq, on the authority of his father, on the authority of `Abdullah ibn Abi al-Hamsa`, who said: I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, before he was sent, and I had some left over for him, so I promised him that I would bring it to him in that place. He said: Then I forgot my day and the next day, so I came to him on the third day while he was in that place, and he said to me: “O young man, you have made it difficult for me. I have been here for three days waiting for you.” This is the wording of al-Kharaiti, and he cited good traces in that regard. Ibn Mandah Abu `Abdullah narrated it in the book Ma`rifat al-Sahaba with his chain of transmission on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Tahman, on the authority of Badil ibn Maysarah, on the authority of `Abd al-Karim, on his authority. Some of them said: He was called the truthful one because he said to his father: You will find me, God willing, among the patient ones. So he was truthful in that, so truthfulness in a promise is one of the praiseworthy qualities, just as its opposite is one of the reprehensible qualities. God Almighty said: O you who have believed, why do you say what you do not do? Great is hatred in the sight of God that you say what you do not do. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks, he lies, when he promises, he breaks his promise, and when he is entrusted, he betrays.” And since these are the qualities of hypocrites, being involved in their opposite is one of the qualities of believers. For this reason, God praised His servant and Messenger Ismail for being truthful in his promise, and likewise the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was also truthful in his promise, and he did not promise anyone anything without fulfilling it. He praised Abu al-‘As ibn al-Rabi’, the husband of his daughter Zaynab, and said: He spoke to me and told me the truth, and he promised me and fulfilled his promise. And when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, died, the Caliph Abu Bakr al-Siddiq said: “Whoever has a promise or debt with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, So let him come to me and I will pay for him. So Jabir bin Abdullah came and said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “If the money of Bahrain came, I would give you this and this and this,” meaning he could fill his two hands. So when the money of Bahrain came, Abu Bakr ordered Jabir to scoop up some of the money with his hands, then he ordered him after him and it was five hundred dirhams, so he gave him twice as much with it. His saying: And he was a messenger and a prophet indicates that Ishmael was more honored than his brother Isaac, because he was only described as a prophet, while Ishmael was described as a prophet and a messenger. It has been proven in Sahih Muslim that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God chose Ishmael from the children of Abraham, and he mentioned the rest of the hadith, which indicates the correctness of what we have said. And his saying: And he used to enjoin prayer and zakat upon his family, and he was pleasing to his Lord. This is also from the beautiful praise and praiseworthy attribute, and the right character, as he was persistent in obeying his Lord, the Almighty, the Majestic, commanding it for his family, as God Almighty said to His Messenger: And enjoin prayer upon your family and be constant therein. And He said: “O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are angels, harsh and severe; they do not disobey God in what He commands them but do what they are commanded.” That is, enjoin them to do good and forbid them from evil and do not leave them careless, lest the Fire consume them on the Day of Resurrection. It was reported in the hadith on the authority of Abu Hurairah that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “May God have mercy on a man who gets up at night, prays, and wakes his wife, and if she refuses, he sprinkles water in her face. May God have mercy on a woman who gets up at night, prays, and wakes her husband, and if he refuses, she sprinkles water in his face.” Narrated by Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah. On the authority of Abu Saeed and Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with them, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: If a man wakes up at night and wakes up his wife and they pray two rak’ahs, they will be recorded among those who remember God often, both men and women. Narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah, and the wording is his.

19:56: Idris, peace be upon him, was mentioned with praise, saying that he was a friend and a prophet, and that God raised him to a high position. It was mentioned in the Sahih that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, passed by him on the night of the Isra’ while he was in the fourth heaven. Ibn Jarir narrated here a strange and amazing trace, saying: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told me, Ibn Wahb informed us, Jarir bin Hazim informed me, on the authority of Sulayman al-A’mash, on the authority of Shammar bin Atiyah, on the authority of Hilal bin Yasaf, who said: Ibn Abbas asked Ka’b while I was present, and he said to him: What is the saying of God the Almighty to Idris, And We raised him to a high station? Ka’b said: As for Idris, God revealed to him that I raise for you every day the equivalent of the deeds of all the children of Adam, so he wanted to increase his deeds, so a close friend of his from the angels came to him and said to him: God revealed to me such and such, so speak to the Angel of Death for me, so let him delay me until I increase my deeds, so he carried him between his wings until he ascended with him to the heaven, and when he was in the fourth heaven, the Angel of Death met them descending, so he spoke to the Angel of Death about what Idris had spoken to him about, and he said: Where is Idris? He said: Here he is on my back. The Angel of Death said: “It is amazing! I was sent and it was said to me: ‘Take the soul of Idris in the fourth heaven.’ I kept saying: ‘How can I take his soul in the fourth heaven while he is on earth?’ So his soul was taken there. This is what God said: ‘And We raised him to a high station.’” This is from the reports of Ka’b al-Ahbar from the Israelite narrations, and some of it is strange, and God knows best. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from another source on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he asked Ka’b and he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above, except that he said to that angel: Would you like to ask him, meaning the Angel of Death, how much of my life remains so that I may increase my deeds, and he mentioned the rest of it. In it: When he asked him about what remained of my life, he said: I do not know until I look, so he looked and then said: You are asking me about a man who has nothing left of his life except the blink of an eye, so the angel looked under his wing and behold, he had taken him, peace be upon him, and he did not notice him, then he narrated it from another source on the authority of Ibn Abbas that Idris was a tailor, and he would not insert a needle except that he would say: Glory be to God, so he would go to bed when he went to bed and there was no one on earth better in deeds than him, and he mentioned the rest of it like the one before it or something similar. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And We raised him to a high station, that Idris was raised but did not die as Jesus was raised. Sufyan said on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Mujahid, And We raised him to a high station, that is, the fourth heaven. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We raised him to a high station, that is, he was raised to the sixth heaven and died there. This is what Ad-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said. Al-Hasan and others said regarding his statement: And We raised him to a high station, that is, Paradise.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from another source on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he asked Ka’b and he mentioned something similar to what was mentioned above, except that he said to that angel: Would you like to ask him, meaning the Angel of Death, how much of my life remains so that I may increase my deeds, and he mentioned the rest of it. In it: When he asked him about what remained of my life, he said: I do not know until I look, so he looked and then said: You are asking me about a man who has nothing left of his life except the blink of an eye, so the angel looked under his wing and behold, he had taken him, peace be upon him, and he did not notice him, then he narrated it from another source on the authority of Ibn Abbas that Idris was a tailor, and he would not insert a needle except that he would say: Glory be to God, so he would go to bed when he went to bed and there was no one on earth better in deeds than him, and he mentioned the rest of it like the one before it or something similar. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid regarding his statement: And We raised him to a high station, that Idris was raised but did not die as Jesus was raised. Sufyan said on the authority of Mansur on the authority of Mujahid, And We raised him to a high station, that is, the fourth heaven. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We raised him to a high station, that is, he was raised to the sixth heaven and died there. This is what Ad-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said. Al-Hasan and others said regarding his statement: And We raised him to a high station, that is, Paradise.
19:58: God Almighty says: These prophets - and not only those mentioned in this surah, but the entire genus of prophets, peace be upon them - he digressed from mentioning individuals to the genus - those upon whom God bestowed favor from among the prophets from the descendants of Adam the verse, as al-Suddi and Ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on them, said. The one he meant from the descendants of Adam was Idris, and the one he meant from the descendants of those whom We carried with Noah was Abraham, and the one he meant from the descendants of Abraham was Isaac, Jacob, and Ishmael, and the one he meant from the descendants of Israel was Moses, Aaron, Zachariah, John, and Jesus, son of Mary. Ibn Jarir said: That is why he separated their lineages, even though Adam is included among them, because among them is one who was not from the descendants of the one who was with Noah in the ship, and he is Idris, for he is the grandfather of Noah. I said This is what is most apparent, that Idris is in the lineage of Noah, peace be upon them both, and it has been said that he is from the prophets of the Children of Israel, taken from the hadith of the Night Journey, where he said in his greeting to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Welcome to the righteous prophet and righteous brother, and he did not say and the righteous son, as Adam and Abraham, peace be upon them both, said. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated: Yunus told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told me on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib on the authority of Abdullah ibn Muhammad that Idris was older than Noah, so God sent him to his people and commanded them to say, There is no god but God, and to do whatever they wanted, but they refused, so God Almighty destroyed them. What supports that this verse refers to the type of prophets is that it is like the words of God Almighty in Surat al-An’am 6:“And that was Our argument which We gave Abraham against his people. We raise by degrees whom We will. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing. And We gave him Isaac and Jacob, each of them We guided. And Noah We guided before. And among his descendants were David and Solomon and Job and Joseph and Moses and Aaron. Thus do We reward the doers of good. And Zachariah and John and Jesus and Elias, all were among the righteous. And Ishmael and Elisha and Jonah and Lot. Each of them We preferred above the worlds. And among their fathers and their descendants and their brothers. And We chose them and guided them to a straight path. That is God guides thereby whom He wills of His servants. And if they had associated others with Him, all that they used to do would have been in vain for them. Those are the ones to whom We have given the Scripture and wisdom and prophethood. But if they disbelieve in it - then We have entrusted it to a people who are not disbelievers in it. Those are the ones whom God has guided, so follow their guidance. And God, the Most High, said: “Some of them We have told you about, and some We have not told you about.” And in Sahih Al-Bukhari, on the authority of Mujahid, he asked Ibn Abbas: Is there a prostration in Sad? He said: Yes. Then he recited this verse: Those are the ones whom God has guided, so follow their guidance. So your Prophet is among those whom He has commanded to follow. He said: And he is one of them, meaning David. God the Almighty said in this noble verse: When the verses of the Most Gracious are recited to them, they fall down in prostration and weeping. That is, when they hear the words of God, which include His arguments, evidence and proofs, they prostrate to their Lord in submission, humility, praise and thanks for the great blessings they have. Baka is the plural of bak, and for this reason the scholars agreed on the legitimacy of prostration here, following their example and their way. Sufyan al-Thawri said, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Muammar, who said: “Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, recited Surah Maryam, prostrated and said: This is the prostration, so where is the weeping?” He meant crying. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir, and the mention of Abu Muammar was omitted from its narrators, as I have seen, and God knows best.”
19:59: When God the Almighty mentioned the party of the happy ones, who are the prophets, peace be upon them, and those who followed them from those who uphold the limits and commands of God, who perform the obligations of God and abandon His prohibitions, He mentioned that there came after them a generation meaning other generations who neglected the prayer. And if they neglected it, then they neglected other obligations, because it is the pillar and foundation of religion and the best deeds of the servants, and they turned to the desires of this world and its pleasures and were satisfied with the life of this world and were content with it, so these will encounter error, meaning loss on the Day of Resurrection. And they differed about what is meant by neglecting the prayer here. Some said: What is meant by neglecting it is abandoning it completely, as Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi and Ibn Zayd ibn Aslam al-Suddi said, and Ibn Jarir chose it. For this reason, some of the predecessors, successors, and imams went as is well-known from Imam Ahmad, and a statement from al-Shafi’i went to declaring the one who neglects the prayer an unbeliever, based on the hadith Between the servant and polytheism is the abandonment of the prayer. The other hadith is: The covenant between us and them is prayer, so whoever abandons it has disbelieved. This is not the place to elaborate on this issue. Al-Awza’i said on the authority of Musa bin Sulayman on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Mukhaymara regarding his statement: Then there came after them a generation who neglected the prayer, he said: meaning they neglected the times. If it was abandonment, it would be disbelief. And Wakee’ said on the authority of Al-Mas’udi on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Abd Al-Rahman and Al-Hasan bin Saad on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud that it was said to him: God mentions prayer frequently in the Qur’an: Those who are heedless of their prayers, “constant in their prayers,” and maintain their prayers. Ibn Mas’ud said: At their times. They said: We did not see that except in abandonment. He said: That is disbelief. Masruq said: No one maintains the five prayers and is written among the heedless. In their excess is destruction, and their excess is wasting them of their time. Al-Awza’i said on the authority of Ibrahim bin Yazid: Umar bin Abdul Aziz recited: “Then there came after them a generation who neglected the prayer and pursued desires. So they are going to meet with error.” Then he said: Their waste was not abandoning it, but they wasted the time. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: Then there came after them a generation who neglected the prayer and pursued desires. He said: When the Hour comes and the righteous people of the nation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, go, they will seduce one another in the alleys. Ibn Jurayj narrated something similar on the authority of Mujahid. Jabir al-Ju’fi narrated on the authority of Mujahid, Ikrimah, and Ata’ bin Abi Rabah that they are from this nation, meaning at the end of time. Ibn Jarir said: Al-Harith told me, Al-Hasan Al-Ashib told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Muhajir, on the authority of Mujahid, Then there came after them a generation who neglected the prayer and followed desires. He said: They are in this nation who will swarm like cattle and donkeys in the streets, they do not fear God in the heavens, nor are they ashamed of people on earth. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Sinan Al-Wasiti told us, Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Muqri told us, Haywah told us, Bashir bin Abi Amr Al-Khawlani told us that Al-Walid bin Qais told him that he heard Abu Sa’id Al-Khudri say: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “There will be a generation after sixty years who will neglect the prayer and follow desires, so they will meet with error. Then there will be a generation who will recite the Qur’an but it will not go beyond their collarbones, and three will recite the Qur’an: a believer, a hypocrite, and a wicked person.” Bashir said: I said to Al-Walid: Who are these three? He said: The believer is the one who believes in it, and the hypocrite is the one who disbelieves in it. And the wicked person eats from it, and this is how Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Muqri. Ibn Abi Hatim also said: My father told me, Ibrahim bin Musa told us, Isa bin Yunus told us, Ubaydullah bin Abd al-Rahman bin Wahb told us, on the authority of Malik, on the authority of Abu al-Rijal, that Aisha used to send something as charity to the people of the Suffa, and she would say: Do not give any of it to a Berber man or woman, for I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “They are the successors about whom God the Most High said: ‘Then there came after them a generation who neglected prayer.’” This hadith is strange. He also said: My father told me, Abd al-Rahman bin al-Dahhak told us, al-Walid told us, Harez told us, on the authority of a sheikh from the people of Medina, that he heard Muhammad bin Ka’b al-Qurazi say about God’s statement: ‘Then there came after them a generation’: The verse: They are the people of the West who rule, but they are worse than any king. Ka'b al-Ahbar said: By God, I find the description of the hypocrites in the Book of God Almighty: Coffee drinkers, neglecting prayers, salivating over Kaabas, sleeping during the dark hours, being excessive in the mornings, neglecting congregational prayers. He said: Then he recited this verse: "Then there came after them a posterity who neglected prayer and pursued desires. So they are going to meet with error." Al-Hasan al-Basri said: They neglected the mosques and stuck to the farms. Abu al-Ashhab al-Attardi said: God revealed to David, peace be upon him: O David, beware and warn your companions against eating desires, for the hearts attached to the desires of this world have their minds veiled from Me. The least I can do to one of My servants if he chooses one of his desires is to deprive him of My obedience. Imam Ahmad said: Zaid bin Al-Habbab told us, Abu Al-Samh Al-Tamimi told us on the authority of Abu Qabil that he heard Uqbah bin Amir say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I fear for my nation two things: the Qur’an and milk.” As for milk, they will follow the countryside and desires and abandon prayer. As for the Qur’an, the hypocrites will learn it and argue with the believers with it. And he narrated it on the authority of Hasan bin Musa on the authority of Ibn Lahi’ah: Abu Qabil told us on the authority of Uqbah on it, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet, with a similar chain of transmission, and he is the only one who transmitted it. And His statement: Then they will meet with Ghayyan Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas Then they will meet Ghayyan meaning loss. Qatada said: Evil. Sufyan al-Thawri, Shu’bah and Muhammad bin Ishaq said on the authority of Abu Ishaq al-Sabi’i on the authority of Abu Ubaidah on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud Then they will meet Ghayyan he said: A valley in Hell with a deep bottom and foul taste. Al-A’mash said on the authority of Ziyad on the authority of Abu Iyad regarding His statement: Then they will meet Ghayyan he said: A valley in Hell of pus and blood. Imam Abu Jaafar bin Jarir said: Abbas bin Abi Talib told me, Muhammad bin Ziyad told us, Sharqi bin Qatami told us on the authority of Luqman bin Amir Al-Khuza’i, who said: I came to Abu Umamah Siddi bin Ajlan Al-Bahili and said: Tell us a hadith that you heard from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. So he called for food, then he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If a rock weighing ten ounces were thrown from the edge of Hell, it would not reach its bottom for fifty autumns, then it would end in a state of confusion and sins. He said: I said: What is confusion and sins? He said: He said: Two wells at the bottom of Hell in which the pus of the people of Hell flows. They are the two that God mentioned in His Book: They neglected the prayer and followed their desires, so they are going to meet a state of confusion. And His statement in al-Furqan 25:nor do they commit adultery, and whoever does that will meet a state of sin. This is a strange hadith and its chain of transmission to the Prophet is denounced. And His saying: Except for he who repents, believes, and does righteousness means except for he who turns from abandoning prayers and following desires, for God accepts his repentance and makes his end good and makes him one of the inheritors of Paradise of bliss. For this reason He said: Then those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged at all, because repentance wipes out what came before it. In another hadith, The one who repents from sin is like one who has no sin. For this reason, these repentant people will not lose anything from the deeds they did, nor will they be compared to what they did before it, so that what they did after it will be lost for them, because that was wasted and forgotten, and was lost for free from the generosity of the Generous and the patience of the Forbearing. This exception here is like His saying in Surat al-Furqan 25:“And those who do not invoke with God another deity or kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse. And whoever should do that will meet a penalty. * The punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein humiliated. * Except for he who repents, believes, and does righteous work. For them God will replace their evil deeds with good. And ever is God Forgiving.” Merciful.

19:61: God the Almighty says: The gardens which those who repent from their sins will enter are the Gardens of Eden, meaning the residence that the Most Gracious promised His servants in the unseen, meaning it is from the unseen in which they believe and have not seen, due to the intensity of their conviction and the strength of their faith. His statement: "Indeed, His promise was to be fulfilled" is an emphasis on the occurrence, confirmation and stability of that, for God does not break His promise or change it, as He says: "His promise was to be fulfilled" meaning it will inevitably happen. His statement here: "Coming" means that the servants are going to Him and will come to Him. Some of them said "coming" means coming, because whatever came to you, you have come to it, just as the Arabs say: Fifty years have come upon me, and I have come upon fifty years, both of them have the same meaning. His saying: They will not hear therein any idle talk, meaning that in these gardens there is no idle, meaningless talk as might be found in this world. His saying: “Except peace” is an interrupted exception like his saying: “They will hear therein no idle talk or sinful speech * Except the saying, ‘Peace, peace.’” And his saying: And they will have their provision therein, morning and evening, meaning at the same time as the mornings and evenings, not that there is night and day, but they will be at times that follow one another and they will know their passing by lights and radiance, as Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The first group to enter Paradise will be like the moon on a full moon night. They will not spit therein, nor blow their noses therein, nor will they defecate. Their utensils and combs will be of gold and silver, their incense burners will be of aloe, and their sweat will be of musk. Each one of them will have two wives, the marrow of whose leg will be seen through the flesh because of the beauty. There will be no difference between them and no hatred. Their hearts will be like the heart of one man. They glorify God morning and evening.” Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim in their Sahihs from the hadith of Muammar. Imam Ahmad said: Yaqub told us, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, Al-Harith bin Fadil Al-Ansari told us, on the authority of Mahmoud bin Labid Al-Ansari, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The martyrs will be on a river at the gate of Paradise in a green dome. Their provision will come out to them from Paradise morning and evening.” Ahmad is the only one to narrate it from this source. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And they will have their provision therein morning and evening. He said: The amounts of the night and the day. Ibn Jarir said: Ali bin Sahm told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us: I asked Zuhair bin Muhammad about the statement of God the Most High: And they will have their provision therein, morning and evening. He said: There is no night in Paradise, they are in light forever and they have the amount of night and day, and they know the amount of night by the lowering of the veils and the closing of the doors, and they know the amount of day by the lifting of the veils and the opening of the doors. And with this chain of transmission on the authority of Al-Walid bin Muslim on the authority of Khalid on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, and he mentioned the gates of Paradise and said: Gates whose exterior can be seen from their interior, so they speak and speak and they understand, open or close and they do. Qatada said about His statement: And they will have their provision therein, morning and evening, there are two hours in it, morning and evening, there is no night or day, but it is light and brightness. Mujahid said: There is neither morning nor evening, but they are given it according to what they desired in this world. Al-Hasan, Qatada and others said: The most luxurious among the Arabs were those who ate lunch and dinner, so the Qur’an was revealed regarding the luxury that was in their souls, so God the Almighty said: And for them is their provision therein, morning and evening. Ibn Mahdi said on the authority of Hammad bin Zaid on the authority of Hisham on the authority of Al-Hasan: And for them is their provision therein, morning and evening. He said: The early morning refers to the evening, and the evening refers to the early morning, there is no night in it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Salim bin Mansour bin Ammar told us, my father told me, Muhammad bin Ziyad, the judge of the people of Shamshat, told me, on the authority of Abdullah bin Hudayr, on the authority of Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There is no morning of the mornings of Paradise - and all of Paradise is mornings - except that a friend of God is brought therein, a wife from the houris, the lowest of them, who was created from saffron.” Abu Muhammad said: This is a strange and rejected hadith. And His statement: This is the Paradise which We give as an inheritance to those of Our servants who were righteous. That is, this Paradise which We have described with these great attributes is the one which We give as an inheritance to Our righteous servants, who are obedient to God Almighty in good times and bad, who suppress anger, and who pardon people, as God Almighty said at the beginning of Surat al-Mu’minun 23:“Indeed, the believers have succeeded. Who are humble in their prayers.” Until He said: “Those are the inheritors. Who will inherit Paradise, wherein they will abide eternally.”
19:62: God the Almighty says: The gardens which those who repent from their sins will enter are the Gardens of Eden, meaning the residence that the Most Gracious promised His servants in the unseen, meaning it is from the unseen in which they believe and have not seen, due to the intensity of their conviction and the strength of their faith. His statement: Indeed, His promise was to be fulfilled is an emphasis on the occurrence, confirmation and stability of that, for God does not break His promise or change it, as He says: His promise was to be fulfilled meaning it will inevitably happen. His statement here: Coming means that the servants are going to Him and will come to Him. Some of them said coming means coming, because whatever came to you, you have come to it, just as the Arabs say: Fifty years have come upon me, and I have come upon fifty years, both of them have the same meaning. His saying: They will not hear therein any idle talk, meaning that in these gardens there is no idle, meaningless talk as might be found in this world. His saying: “Except peace” is an interrupted exception like his saying: “They will hear therein no idle talk or sinful speech * Except the saying, ‘Peace, peace.’” And his saying: And they will have their provision therein, morning and evening, meaning at the same time as the mornings and evenings, not that there is night and day, but they will be at times that follow one another and they will know their passing by lights and radiance, as Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The first group to enter Paradise will be like the moon on a full moon night. They will not spit therein, nor blow their noses therein, nor will they defecate. Their utensils and combs will be of gold and silver, their incense burners will be of aloe, and their sweat will be of musk. Each one of them will have two wives, the marrow of whose leg will be seen through the flesh because of the beauty. There will be no difference between them and no hatred. Their hearts will be like the heart of one man. They glorify God morning and evening.” Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim in their Sahihs from the hadith of Muammar. Imam Ahmad said: Yaqub told us, my father told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, Al-Harith bin Fadil Al-Ansari told us, on the authority of Mahmoud bin Labid Al-Ansari, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The martyrs will be on a river at the gate of Paradise in a green dome. Their provision will come out to them from Paradise morning and evening.” Ahmad is the only one to narrate it from this source. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And they will have their provision therein morning and evening. He said: The amounts of the night and the day. Ibn Jarir said: Ali bin Sahm told us, Al-Walid bin Muslim told us: I asked Zuhair bin Muhammad about the statement of God the Most High: And they will have their provision therein, morning and evening. He said: There is no night in Paradise, they are in light forever and they have the amount of night and day, and they know the amount of night by the lowering of the veils and the closing of the doors, and they know the amount of day by the lifting of the veils and the opening of the doors. And with this chain of transmission on the authority of Al-Walid bin Muslim on the authority of Khalid on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri, and he mentioned the gates of Paradise and said: Gates whose exterior can be seen from their interior, so they speak and speak and they understand, open or close and they do. Qatada said about His statement: And they will have their provision therein, morning and evening, there are two hours in it, morning and evening, there is no night or day, but it is light and brightness. Mujahid said: There is neither morning nor evening, but they are given it according to what they desired in this world. Al-Hasan, Qatada and others said: The most luxurious among the Arabs were those who ate lunch and dinner, so the Qur’an was revealed regarding the luxury that was in their souls, so God the Almighty said: And for them is their provision therein, morning and evening. Ibn Mahdi said on the authority of Hammad bin Zaid on the authority of Hisham on the authority of Al-Hasan: And for them is their provision therein, morning and evening. He said: The early morning refers to the evening, and the evening refers to the early morning, there is no night in it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein told us, Salim bin Mansour bin Ammar told us, my father told me, Muhammad bin Ziyad, the judge of the people of Shamshat, told me, on the authority of Abdullah bin Hudayr, on the authority of Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “There is no morning of the mornings of Paradise - and all of Paradise is mornings - except that a friend of God is brought therein, a wife from the houris, the lowest of them, who was created from saffron.” Abu Muhammad said: This is a strange and rejected hadith. And His statement: This is the Paradise which We give as an inheritance to those of Our servants who were righteous. That is, this Paradise which We have described with these great attributes is the one which We give as an inheritance to Our righteous servants, who are obedient to God Almighty in good times and bad, who suppress anger, and who pardon people, as God Almighty said at the beginning of Surat al-Mu’minun 23:“Indeed, the believers have succeeded. Who are humble in their prayers.” Until He said: “Those are the inheritors. Who will inherit Paradise, wherein they will abide eternally.” The believer says to them: What is wrong with me that I call you to salvation, which is the worship of God alone, with no partner, and the belief in His Messenger whom God sent? “And you invite me to the Fire. You invite me to disbelieve in God and associate with Him that of which I have no knowledge.” That is, out of ignorance and without proof. And I invite you to the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving. That is, He, in His might and pride, forgives the sin of whoever repents to Him. Indeed, you invite me to it. He says, Truly? Al-Suddi and Ibn Jarir said that the meaning of his saying, Indeed, you invite me to it is truly. Ad-Dahhak said, No crime, meaning, no lie. Ali ibn Abi Talha said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, No crime, meaning, Yes, that to which you call me of idols and rivals, ‘He has no call in this world or in the Hereafter.’ Mujahid said, The idol has nothing. Qatadah said, It means that the idol neither benefits nor harms. As-Suddi said, It does not answer its caller, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. This is like the statement of God, the Most High, “And who is more astray than he who calls upon others besides God, who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they, of their call, are unaware? And when the people are gathered together, they will be enemies to them and will be disbelievers in their worship.” If you call upon them, they will not hear your call, and if they heard, they would not respond to you. And His statement, And that our return is to God, meaning in the Hereafter, so He will reward each one according to his deeds. For this reason, He said, And that the transgressors are the companions of the Fire, meaning, they will abide therein forever because of their transgression, which is their associating partners with God, the Almighty. Then you will remember what I say to you, meaning, you will know the truth of what I have commanded you to do and what I have forbidden you from doing. I advised you and made it clear to you, and you remember it and regret it when regret is of no use. And I entrust my affair to God, meaning I put my trust in God and seek His help, and I boycott you and keep you away. Indeed, God is Seeing of His servants, meaning He is Seeing of them, the Most High and Most Holy. He guides whomever deserves guidance and misguides whomever deserves misguidance. He has the conclusive argument, perfect wisdom, and effective power. And the saying of God, the Most High: So God saved him from the evil of their plotting meaning in this world and the Hereafter. As for this world, God saved him with Moses, peace be upon him, and as for the Hereafter, he will be in Paradise. And the people of Pharaoh were encompassed by an evil punishment meaning drowning in the sea and then being transferred from it to Hell. Their souls will be exposed to the Fire morning and evening until the Day of Resurrection. So when the Day of Resurrection comes, their souls and bodies will be gathered together in the Fire. For this reason, He said: And on the Day the Hour appears, admit Pharaoh’s people into the severest punishment meaning the most painful and the greatest punishment. This verse is a major basis for the Sunnis’ evidence for the torment of the intermediate realm in the graves, and it is the saying of God, the Most High: The Fire they will be exposed to morning and evening. But here is a question, which is that there is no doubt that this verse is Meccan, and they used it as evidence for the torment of the grave in the Barzakh. Imam Ahmad said: Hashim told us, he is Ibn Al-Qasim Abu Al-Nadr, Ishaq Ibn Saeed, he is Ibn Amr Ibn Saeed Ibn Al-As, Saeed told us, meaning his father, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that a Jewish woman used to serve her, and whenever Aisha, may God be pleased with her, did anything good for her, the Jewish woman would say to her, May God protect you from the torment of the grave. She, may God be pleased with her, said: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to me, and I said: O Messenger of God, is there a torment in the grave before the Day of Resurrection? He, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No, who claims that? This Jewess said, I will not do her any good deed except that she will say, ‘May God protect you from the punishment of the grave.’ The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, “The Jews lied, and they are the biggest liar to God. There is no punishment before the Day of Resurrection.” Then he stayed for as long as God willed him to stay. Then one day he came out at noon, covered with his garment, his eyes red, and he was calling out at the top of his voice, “The grave is like pieces of a dark night. O people, if you knew what I know, you would weep much and laugh little. O people, seek refuge in God from the punishment of the grave, for the punishment of the grave is true.” This is a sound chain of transmission according to the criteria of Bukhari and Muslim, but they did not include it. Ahmad narrated that Yazid told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha may God be pleased with her, who said, “A Jewish woman asked her for something, and she gave it to her. She said to her, ‘May God protect you from the punishment of the grave.’ Aisha may God be pleased with her did not approve of that, but when she saw the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), she said to him, and he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, ‘No.’ Aisha may God be pleased with her said, “The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) then said to us after that, ‘It has been revealed to me that you will be tested in your graves.’” This also according to their criteria. It is said: What is the connection between this and the fact that the verse was revealed in Mecca and that it contains evidence of the torment of the intermediate realm? The answer is that the verse indicates that the souls are exposed to the Fire morning and evening in the intermediate realm. It does not indicate that their pain is connected to their bodies in the graves, as this might be specific to the soul. As for the occurrence of this in the intermediate realm for the body and its pain because of it, this is only indicated by the Sunnah in the acceptable hadiths mentioned below. It may be said that this verse only indicates the torment of the disbelievers in the intermediate realm, and this does not necessarily mean that the believer will be tormented in his grave for a sin. Evidence of this is what Imam Ahmad narrated: Uthman bin Umar narrated to us, Yunus narrated to us, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon her and there was a Jewish woman with her, and she was saying, Do you know that you will be tested in your graves? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was startled and said, Only the Jews will be tested. Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said, “We stayed for a few nights, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, “Behold, you will be tested in the graves.” Aisha, may God be pleased with her, said, “Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would seek refuge from the torment of the grave.” Muslim narrated it in this way, on the authority of Harun bin Saeed and Harmalah, both of them on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Yunus bin Yazid Al-Ayli, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on his authority. It may be said that this verse indicates the torment of the souls in the intermediate realm, but it does not necessarily mean that it is connected to the bodies in their graves. So when the revelation was sent to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) concerning that in particular, he sought refuge from it, and God knows best. Al-Bukhari narrated from the hadeeth of Shu’bah, from Ash’ath ibn Abi Ash-Sha’tha’, from his father, from Masruq, from Aisha may God be pleased with her, that a Jewish woman entered upon her and said, We seek refuge in God from the torment of the grave. Aisha may God be pleased with her asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) about the torment of the grave, and he (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said, Yes, the torment of the grave is true. Aisha may God be pleased with her said, “I never saw the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) pray a prayer after that without seeking refuge from the torment of the grave.” This indicates that he, may God bless him and grant him peace, hastened to believe the Jewish report and decided upon it. In the previous report, he denied it until the revelation came to him, so perhaps they are two issues, and God Almighty knows best. The hadiths about the torment of the grave are very numerous. Qatada said about the Almighty’s statement: morning and evening morning and evening as long as the world remains, it will be said to them, O family of Pharaoh, these are your dwellings, as a rebuke, punishment, and humiliation for them. Ibn Zayd said, They are in it today, being taken to and from until the Hour comes. He said: Ibn Abi Hatim told us, Abu Saeed told us, Al-Maharbi told us, Laith told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Tharwan, on the authority of Hudhayl, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, may God be pleased with him, who said: The souls of the martyrs are in the bodies of green birds that roam with them in Paradise wherever they wish. The souls of the children of the believers are in the bodies of sparrows that roam in Paradise wherever they wish and take refuge in lamps suspended from the Throne. The souls of the family of Pharaoh are in the bodies of black birds that go to Hell in the morning and in the evening, and that is its width. Al-Thawri narrated it on the authority of Abu Qais on the authority of Hudhayl bin Shurahbil from his words about the souls of the family of Pharaoh, and Al-Suddi said the same. In the hadith of Isra’ narrated by Abu Harun al-Abdi on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he said: “Then I was taken to a large group of God’s creation, men, each of whose stomach was like a huge house, chained to the path of the family of Pharaoh, and the family of Pharaoh were exposed to the Fire morning and evening. ‘And on the Day the Hour is established, admit the family of Pharaoh into the severest punishment.’ And the family of Pharaoh are like branded camels, striking stones and trees and not understanding.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn told us, Zayd ibn Akram told us, Aamer ibn Mudrik al-Harithi told us, Utbah told us - meaning Ibn Yaqzan - on the authority of Qays ibn Muslim, on the authority of Tariq, on the authority of Shihab, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: No one who does good, whether Muslim or disbeliever, does it well except that God Almighty will reward him. We said: O Messenger of God, what is God’s reward for the disbeliever? He said: If he has maintained family ties or given charity or done a good deed, God Almighty will reward him with wealth, children, health, and the like. We said: So what… His reward in the Hereafter? He (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: A punishment less severe than this punishment. Then he recited: Enter the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment. Al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad on the authority of Zayd ibn Akram, then he said: We do not know of any other chain of narration for it other than this. Ibn Jarir said: Abdul-Karim ibn Abi ‘Umayr told us: Hammad ibn Muhammad al-Fazari al-Balkhi told us: I heard al-Awza’i when a man asked him: May God have mercy on you. We saw birds coming out of the sea and heading towards the west, eggs in groups. No one knows their number except God, the Exalted. Then when it was dusk, the same number would return black. He said: Did you realise that? He said: Yes. He said: Those birds have in their crops the souls of Pharaoh’s family. They are shown to the Fire morning and evening, and they return to their nests with their feathers burned and turned black. Then white feathers grow on them at night and the black ones scatter. Then they go to the Fire morning and evening, and then they return to their nests. That is their way in this world. When the Day of Resurrection comes, God the Most High will say: Enter the family of Pharaoh into the severest punishment. He said: And they used to say that they were six hundred thousand fighters. Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq told us, Malik told us, from Nafi’, from Ibn ‘Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When one of you dies, his seat is shown to him morning and evening. If he is from the people of Paradise, then he is from the people of Paradise, and if he is from the people of Hell, then he is from the people of Hell. Then it is said: This is your seat until God the Almighty raises you to it on the Day of Resurrection.” They narrated it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Malik with it.
