19:64: Imam Ahmad said: Ya`la and Waki` told us: Umar ibn Dhir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Gabriel: What prevents you from visiting us more often than you do? He said: Then the verse was revealed: We do not descend except by the command of your Lord until the end of the verse. Al-Bukhari is the only one who narrated it. He narrated it when interpreting this verse on the authority of Abu Na`im on the authority of `Umar ibn Dhar. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of `Umar ibn Dhar. They have an addition at the end of the hadith. This was the answer to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-`Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Gabriel was detained from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was distressed by this and was saddened. Gabriel came to him and said: O Muhammad, We do not descend except by the command of your Lord verse. Mujahid said: Gabriel stayed with Muhammad (peace be upon him) for twelve nights, and they say less. When he came to him, he said: O Gabriel, you stayed with me until the polytheists had every suspicion. Then the verse We do not descend except by the command of your Lord was revealed. He said: This verse is like the one in Ad-Duha, and Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim, Qatadah, As-Suddi and others said the same: It was revealed about Gabriel’s delay. Al-Hakam bin Abaan said on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: “Gabriel delayed descending to the Prophet (peace be upon him) for forty days, then he descended and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said to him: You did not descend until I longed for you. Gabriel said to him: Rather, I longed for you more, but I am commanded. So God revealed to Gabriel to say to him: “We do not descend except by the command of your Lord” the verse. Ibn Abi Hatim may God have mercy on him narrated it, and it is strange.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Sinan told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us on the authority of Mujahid, who said: “The messengers were slow to come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then Gabriel came to him and said to him: What kept you, O Gabriel? Gabriel said to him: How can we come to you when you do not cut your nails, clean your fingernails, trim your moustaches, or use siwaks. Then he recited: ‘We do not descend except by the command of your Lord’ until the end of the verse.” Al-Tabarani said: Abu Amir al-Nahwi told us, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Suri told us, Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Dimashqi told us, Ismail ibn Ayyash told us, Tha’laba ibn Muslim told me on the authority of Abu Ka’b, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “that Gabriel was slow to come to him and mentioned that to him, so he said: How can that be when you do not clean your teeth, nor trim your nails, nor cut your moustaches, nor clean your fingernails?” And thus Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Abu al-Yaman on the authority of Ismail ibn Ayyash on the authority of Ibn Abbas, in a similar manner. Imam Ahmad said: Sayyar told us, Ja’far ibn Sulayman told us, Al-Mughira ibn Habib told us on the authority of Malik ibn Dinar, an old man from the people of Madinah told me on the authority of Umm Salamah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Set the assembly straight for us, for an angel will descend to the earth who has never descended to it before. And his statement: He has what is before us and what is behind us It was said: What is meant is what is before us is the matter of this world, and what is behind us is the matter of the Hereafter, and what is between that is between the two blasts. This is the statement of Abu Al-Aliyah, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, and Qatadah in a narration from them, and Al-Suddi and Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas. It was said: What is before us is what is to come of the matter of the Hereafter, and what is behind us meaning what has passed of this world, and what is between that meaning what is between this world and the Hereafter. Something similar was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj, and Ath-Thawri, and Ibn Jarir also chose it, and God knows best. And his saying: And your Lord is not forgetful. Mujahid said that its meaning is that your Lord has not forgotten you. It was previously mentioned that this verse is like his saying: By the forenoon, and by the night when it is still, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He become displeased. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yazid bin Muhammad bin Abdul Samad Al-Dimashqi told us, Muhammad bin Uthman - meaning Abu Al-Jamahir - told us, Ismail bin Ayyash told us, Asim bin Raja bin Haywah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Al-Darda, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, who said: “Whatever God has permitted in His Book is permissible, and whatever He has forbidden is forbidden, and whatever He has remained silent about is a pardon, so accept the pardon of God, for God does not forget anything.” Then he recited this verse: And your Lord is not forgetful. And His statement: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, meaning the Creator of that, its Manager, the Ruler in it, and the Disposer of His judgment, whose judgment cannot be questioned. “So worship Him and be steadfast in His worship. Do you know of any other similar to Him?” Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Do you know of any likeness or similarity for the Lord? And Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr, Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj, and others said the same. And Ikrimah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: No one is called the Most Gracious except Him, blessed and exalted be He, and His name is sanctified.
19:65: Imam Ahmad said: Ya`la and Waki` told us: Umar ibn Dhir told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to Gabriel: What prevents you from visiting us more often than you do? He said: Then the verse was revealed: We do not descend except by the command of your Lord until the end of the verse. Al-Bukhari is the only one who narrated it. He narrated it when interpreting this verse on the authority of Abu Na`im on the authority of `Umar ibn Dhar. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of `Umar ibn Dhar. They have an addition at the end of the hadith. This was the answer to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Al-`Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Gabriel was detained from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was distressed by this and was saddened. Gabriel came to him and said: O Muhammad, We do not descend except by the command of your Lord verse. Mujahid said: Gabriel stayed with Muhammad (peace be upon him) for twelve nights, and they say less. When he came to him, he said: O Gabriel, you stayed with me until the polytheists had every suspicion. Then the verse We do not descend except by the command of your Lord was revealed. He said: This verse is like the one in Ad-Duha, and Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim, Qatadah, As-Suddi and others said the same: It was revealed about Gabriel’s delay. Al-Hakam bin Abaan said on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: “Gabriel delayed descending to the Prophet (peace be upon him) for forty days, then he descended and the Prophet (peace be upon him) said to him: You did not descend until I longed for you. Gabriel said to him: Rather, I longed for you more, but I am commanded. So God revealed to Gabriel to say to him: “We do not descend except by the command of your Lord” the verse. Ibn Abi Hatim may God have mercy on him narrated it, and it is strange.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad bin Sinan told us, Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us on the authority of Mujahid, who said: “The messengers were slow to come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, then Gabriel came to him and said to him: What kept you, O Gabriel? Gabriel said to him: How can we come to you when you do not cut your nails, clean your fingernails, trim your moustaches, or use siwaks. Then he recited: ‘We do not descend except by the command of your Lord’ until the end of the verse.” Al-Tabarani said: Abu Amir al-Nahwi told us, Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Suri told us, Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Dimashqi told us, Ismail ibn Ayyash told us, Tha’laba ibn Muslim told me on the authority of Abu Ka’b, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “that Gabriel was slow to come to him and mentioned that to him, so he said: How can that be when you do not clean your teeth, nor trim your nails, nor cut your moustaches, nor clean your fingernails?” And thus Imam Ahmad narrated it on the authority of Abu al-Yaman on the authority of Ismail ibn Ayyash on the authority of Ibn Abbas, in a similar manner. Imam Ahmad said: Sayyar told us, Ja’far ibn Sulayman told us, Al-Mughira ibn Habib told us on the authority of Malik ibn Dinar, an old man from the people of Madinah told me on the authority of Umm Salamah who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to me: Set the assembly straight for us, for an angel will descend to the earth who has never descended to it before. And his statement: He has what is before us and what is behind us It was said: What is meant is what is before us is the matter of this world, and what is behind us is the matter of the Hereafter, and what is between that is between the two blasts. This is the statement of Abu Al-Aliyah, Ikrimah, Mujahid, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, and Qatadah in a narration from them, and Al-Suddi and Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas. It was said: What is before us is what is to come of the matter of the Hereafter, and what is behind us meaning what has passed of this world, and what is between that meaning what is between this world and the Hereafter. Something similar was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Ad-Dahhak, Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj, and Ath-Thawri, and Ibn Jarir also chose it, and God knows best. And his saying: And your Lord is not forgetful. Mujahid said that its meaning is that your Lord has not forgotten you. It was previously mentioned that this verse is like his saying: By the forenoon, and by the night when it is still, your Lord has not forsaken you, nor has He become displeased. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yazid bin Muhammad bin Abdul Samad Al-Dimashqi told us, Muhammad bin Uthman - meaning Abu Al-Jamahir - told us, Ismail bin Ayyash told us, Asim bin Raja bin Haywah told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Al-Darda, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, who said: “Whatever God has permitted in His Book is permissible, and whatever He has forbidden is forbidden, and whatever He has remained silent about is a pardon, so accept the pardon of God, for God does not forget anything.” Then he recited this verse: And your Lord is not forgetful. And His statement: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, meaning the Creator of that, its Manager, the Ruler in it, and the Disposer of His judgment, whose judgment cannot be questioned. “So worship Him and be steadfast in His worship. Do you know of any other similar to Him?” Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Do you know of any likeness or similarity for the Lord? And Mujahid, Saeed bin Jubayr, Qatadah, Ibn Jurayj, and others said the same. And Ikrimah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: No one is called the Most Gracious except Him, blessed and exalted be He, and His name is sanctified.
19:66: The Almighty tells about man that he is amazed and rules out his return after his death, as the Almighty said: "And if you are amazed, then amazed is their saying: 'When we are dust, shall we then be in a new creation?'" And He said: "Has not man seen that We created him from a sperm-drop? Then at once he is a clear adversary. * And he presents to Us an example and forgets his creation. He says: Who will give life to the bones when they have decayed? * Say: He will give life to them who produced them the first time. And He is Knowing of all creation." And He said here: "And man says: 'When I die, will I then be brought forth alive?' Or does man not remember that We created him before, while he was nothing?'" The Almighty uses the beginning as evidence for the return, meaning that the Almighty created man when he was nothing, so will He not return him when he has become something, as the Almighty said: And it is He who begins creation and then repeats it, and that is easier for Him. And in the Sahih, "God the Almighty says: The son of Adam denied Me, and he had no right to deny Me, and the son of Adam harmed Me, and he had no right to harm Me. As for his denial of Me, it is his saying: He will not return me as He began me, and it is not The first of creation is easier for me than the last. As for his harm to me, it is his saying, I have a son, and I am the One, the Self-Sufficient, Who neither begets nor is begotten, and there is none comparable to Him. And His statement: "By your Lord, We will surely gather them and the devils," the Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, swore by His noble Self that He would inevitably gather them all and their devils whom they used to worship other than God. "Then We will surely bring them around Hell on their knees." Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He means sitting, as in His statement: "And you will see every nation kneeling." Al-Suddi said regarding His statement on their knees: He means standing. A similar statement was narrated on the authority of Marra on the authority of Ibn Masoud. And His statement: "Then We will surely extract from every sect" means from every nation. Mujahid said: "Then He will detain the first for the last until the number is complete, He will bring them all, then He will begin with the greatest and the greatest in crime, and this is His statement: Then We will surely extract from every sect the greatest of them in rebellion against the Most Merciful. Qatada said: Then We will surely extract from every sect those of them who were most rebellious against the Most Merciful. He said: Then We will extract from the people of every religion their leaders and chiefs in evil. Ibn Jurayj and more than one of the early Muslims said the same. This is like the saying of God the Almighty: “Until, when they have all overtaken them therein, the last of them will say to the first of them, ‘Our Lord, these led us astray, so give them a double punishment in the Fire.’ He will say to each one, ‘Doubtless,’ but you do not know. And the first of them will say to the last of them, ‘You had no superiority over us. So taste the punishment for what you used to earn.’” And His saying: Then We are most knowing of those who are most deserving of it to be burned. Then here the report is connected to the report, and what is meant is that God the Almighty is most knowing of those of His servants who deserve to be burned in the fire of Hell and to remain there forever, and of those who deserve to have the punishment doubled, as He said in the previous verse: He will say to each one, ‘Doubtless,’ but you do not know.

19:71: Imam Ahmad said: Sulayman ibn Harb told us, Ghalib ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of Katheer ibn Ziyad al-Barsani, on the authority of Abu Sumayyah, who said: We differed about the entrances. Some of us said: No believer will enter it, and some of us said: They will all enter it, then God will save those who feared God. So I met Jabir ibn Abdullah and said to him: We differed about the entrances. He said: They will all enter it, and Sulayman ibn Murrah said: They will all enter it, and he pointed to his ears with his fingers and said: I would have been silent if I had not heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: “No pious wicked person will remain except that he will enter it, so it will be cool and safe for the believer as the fire was for Abraham, until the fire makes a noise because of their coolness. Then God will save those who feared God and leave the wrongdoers in it on their knees.” Strange and they did not include it. Al-Hasan bin Arafa said: Marwan bin Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Bakkar bin Abi Marwan, on the authority of Khalid bin Ma’dan, who said: The people of Paradise said after they entered Paradise: Did not our Lord promise us to pass through the Fire? He said: You passed by it while it was extinguished. Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Qays bin Abi Hazim, who said: Abdullah bin Rawahah was placing his head on his wife’s lap, and he cried, so his wife cried, so he said: What makes you cry? She said: I saw you crying, so I cried, so he said: I remembered the words of God, the Almighty, And there is not one of you but will pass over it, and I do not know whether I will be saved from it or not - and in another narration: And he was sick. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Malik bin Mughul, on the authority of Abu Ishaq: Whenever Abu Maysarah went to bed, he would say: I wish my mother had not given birth to me, then he would cry. So it was said to him: What makes you cry, Abu Maysarah? He said: We were told that we will enter it, but we were not told that we will leave it. Abdullah bin Mubarak said on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that a man said to his brother: Has it come to you that you will enter Hell? He said: Yes. He said: Has it come to you that you will leave it? He said: No. He said: Then why are you laughing? He said: He was never seen laughing until he met God. Abdul Razzaq also said: Ibn Uyaynah told us on the authority of Amr, he told me that he heard Ibn Abbas arguing with Nafi’ ibn al-Azraq, so Ibn Abbas said: Wurood means entering. Nafi’ said: No. So Ibn Abbas recited: “Indeed, you and what you worship besides God are fuel for Hell. You will be entering it.” And whether they were entered or not, and he said: He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and will lead them to the Fire. Was he entered or not? As for you and I, we will enter it. So see if we will get out of it or not. And I do not see that God will get you out of it by your denial. So Nafi’ laughed. Ibn Jurayj narrated on the authority of Ata’ who said: Abu Rashid al-Haruri, who is Nafi’ ibn al-Azraq, said: They do not hear its hissing sound. Ibn Abbas said: Woe to you! Are you mad? Where is His statement: He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them to the Fire, “And We will drive the criminals to Hell in droves,” And there is not one of you but will pass over it, by God, if the supplication of those who have passed away was: O God, take me out of the Fire unharmed and admit me into Paradise as a gainer. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Maharibi told me, Asbat told us, on the authority of Abdul-Malik, on the authority of Ubaydullah, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: I was with Ibn Abbas when a man called Abu Rashid, who is Nafi’ ibn al-Azraq, came to him and said to him: O Ibn Abbas, what do you think of the statement of God: “And there is not one of you but will pass over it: this is upon your Lord an inevitability decreed”? He said: As for you and me, O Abu Rashid, we will pass over it, so see if we will depart from it or not? Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu’bah said: Abdullah bin al-Sa’ib informed me on the authority of someone who heard Ibn Abbas recite it: There is not one of you but will pass over it, meaning the disbelievers. This is how Umar bin al-Walid al-Shanni narrated that he heard Ikrimah recite it like this: There is not one of you but will pass over it, meaning the unbelievers. He said: “And they are the oppressors. This is how we used to recite it.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: His statement: There is not one of you but will pass over it, meaning the righteous and the wicked. Do you not hear the statement of God to Pharaoh: He will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and will lead them to the Fire, the verse, And We will drive the criminals to Hell, in droves, so He called entering the Fire entering and not coming out. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah, who is Ibn Mas’ud, And there is not one of you but will pass over it. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: All people will pass over it, then they will depart from it with their deeds. Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Abd ibn Hamid, on the authority of Ubayd God, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of al-Suddi, on his authority. And he narrated it on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. This is how this hadith appears here, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. Asbat narrated from Al-Suddi from Marra from Abdullah bin Masoud who said: All people will pass through the Sirat, and their passage will be like their standing around the Fire. Then they will leave the Sirat with their deeds. Some of them will pass like lightning, some like the wind, some like birds, some like the best horses, some like the best camels, and some like the fastest man. The last of them to pass will be a man whose light will be where the big toes of his feet are. He will pass and the Sirat will be overturned. The Sirat is a slippery slope with thorns on it like the thorns of a thorn bush. Its two edges are angels with hooks of fire with which they snatch people. He mentioned the rest of the hadith. It was narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. Ibn Jarir said: Khallad bin Aslam told us, Al-Nadr told us, Israel told us, Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah, regarding his statement: And there is not one of you but will pass over it, he said: The path over Hell is like the edge of a sword. The first layer will pass like lightning, the second like the wind, the third like the best of horses, and the fourth like the best of beasts. Then they will pass and the angels will say: O God, save, save. There is evidence for this in the two Sahihs and others from the narrations of Anas, Abu Saeed, Abu Hurairah, Jabir, and others from the Companions, may God be pleased with them. Ibn Jarir said: Yaqub told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Al-Jariri, on the authority of Abu Al-Salil, on the authority of Ghanim bin Qais, who said: They mentioned the arrival at Hellfire, and Ka’b said: The Hellfire will seize the people as if it were the back of a sack until the feet of all creatures are level on it, the righteous and the wicked. Then a crier will call out to it: Hold back your companions and leave my companions. It will swallow up every guardian of its, and it knows them better than a man knows his own child. The believers will emerge with their clothes wet. Ka’b said: The distance between the shoulders of the treasurer of its treasurers is a year’s journey, with each one of them is a two-pronged column, with which he pushes and by which he will throw seven hundred thousand into Hellfire. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Umm Mubashar, on the authority of Hafsah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I hope that, God willing, no one who witnessed Badr and Al-Hudaybiyyah will enter the Fire. She said: “I said: Doesn’t God say: ‘There is not one of you but will pass over it?’” She said: “I heard Him say: ‘Then We will save those who feared God and leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees.’” Ahmad also said: Ibn Idris told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Abu Sufyan, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Umm Mubashar, the wife of Zayd ibn Haritha, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Hafsah’s house and said: No one who witnessed Badr and Al-Hudaybiyyah will enter the Fire. Hafsah said: Didn’t God say, There is not one of you but will pass over it? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Then We will save those who feared God the verse. In the two Sahihs, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: No one among the Muslims will die three children and be touched by the Fire, except for the oath. Abdul Razzaq said: Muammar told me that Al-Zuhri told me on the authority of Ibn Al-Musayyab on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever has three children die, the Fire will not touch him except by fulfilling an oath. He meant entering it. Abu Dawud Al-Tayalisi said: Zama’ah told us on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Saeed Ibn Al-Musayyab on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: A Muslim will not have three children die and the Fire will not touch him except by fulfilling an oath. Al-Zuhri said: It seems that he meant this verse: “And there is not one of you but will pass over it: this is upon your Lord an inevitability decreed.” Ibn Jarir said: Imran Ibn Bakkar Al-Kila’i told me: Abu Al-Mughira told us: Abd Al-Rahman Ibn Yazid Ibn Tamim told us: Ismail Ibn Ubaidullah told us on the authority of Abu Salih on the authority of Abu Hurayrah who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to visit one of his companions and he was with him. Then he said: God Almighty says: It is My Fire which I send upon My believing servant so that it will be his share of the Fire in the Hereafter.” It is strange and they did not narrate it from this source. Abu Kuraib narrated to us, Ibn Yaman narrated to us, on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Aswad, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Fever is the portion of every believer from the Fire. Then he recited: And there is none of you but will pass over it. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan narrated to us, Ibn Lahi’ah narrated to us, Zaban ibn Fa’id narrated to us, on the authority of Sahl ibn Mu’adh ibn Anas al-Juhani, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: Whoever recites Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad until he completes it ten times, God will build for him a palace in Paradise. Umar said: Then shall we ask for more, O Messenger of God? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God is more numerous and better. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever recites a thousand verses in the cause of God will be recorded on the Day of Resurrection with the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. What excellent companions are those, God willing. And whoever guards behind the Muslims in the cause of God, voluntarily, not for the reward of a ruler, will not see the Fire with his own eyes, except by fulfilling the oath.” God, the Most High, said: And there is none of you but will pass over it. And remembrance in the cause of God is multiplied seven hundred times more than spending. In another narration, seven hundred thousand times. Abu Dawud narrated on the authority of Abu al-Tahir, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Yahya ibn Ayoub, both of them on the authority of Zaban, on the authority of Sahl, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, Indeed, prayer, fasting, and remembrance of God are multiplied seven hundred times over spending in the way of God. Abd al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatadah, regarding his statement, And there is not one of you but will pass over it, he said: He is the one who passes over it. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said regarding his statement, And there is not one of you but will pass over it, he said: The Muslims passing over the bridge in its midst and the polytheists passing over it to enter it. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Those who slip and fall on that day will be many, and two rows of angels will surround the bridge on that day, their supplication being, ‘O God, save, save.’ Al-Suddi said on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, regarding his statement, It was a decree that was decreed upon your Lord, he said: A binding portion. Mujahid said: Definitely, he said: Decree, and Ibn Jurayj said the same. And His saying: Then We will save those who feared God means when all of creation passes by the Fire and those who have fallen from the disbelievers and the sinners who have committed sins fall into it according to their deeds, God the Most High will save the believing righteous from it according to their deeds, so their crossing over the Bridge and their speed will be according to the deeds they did in this world, then they will intercede for the believers who have committed major sins, so the angels, prophets and believers will intercede and bring out many people whom the Fire has consumed except for the circles of their faces, which are the places of prostration, and their bringing them out of the Fire according to what is in their hearts of faith, so they will bring out first the one who had in his heart the weight of a dinar of faith, then the one who comes after him, then the one who comes after him, then the one who comes after him, until they bring out the one who had in his heart the slightest, slightest, smallest weight of an atom of faith, then God will bring out from the Fire whoever said one day in the world: There is no god but God, even if he never did any good, and no one will remain in the Fire except the one who is obligated to remain eternally, as was mentioned in the authentic hadiths from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. For this reason God the Most High said: Then We will save those who feared God, but We will leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees.

So it was said to him: What makes you cry, Abu Maysarah? He said: We were told that we will enter it, but we were not told that we will leave it. He said: Has it come to you that you will leave it? He said: No. He said: Then why are you laughing? He said: He was never seen laughing until he met God. He said: As for you and me, O Abu Rashid, we will pass over it, so see if we will depart from it or not? He said: “And they are the oppressors. This is how we used to recite it.” Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of al-Suddi, on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah, who is Ibn Mas’ud, And there is not one of you but will pass over it. 19:73: The Almighty tells about the disbelievers when the verses of God are recited to them, with clear evidence, evident proof, and clear evidence, that they turn away and turn away from that and say about those who believed, boasting to them and arguing for the truth of what they are upon of the false religion, that they are the best in position and the best in company, meaning the best in status, the most elevated in status, and the best in company, which is the gathering place of men for the hadith, meaning their club is more populous and has more visitors and visitors, meaning, so how can we be in this position upon falsehood and those who are hidden and concealed in the house of Al-Arqam bin Abi Al-Arqam and similar houses upon the truth, as the Almighty said, informing about them: “And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, ‘If it had been good, they would not have preceded us to it. ’” And the people of Noah said, Should we believe in you while the most vile have followed you? And the Almighty said: And thus We have tried some of them with others so that they may say, ‘Are these among us upon whom God has bestowed favor? Is not God most knowing of the grateful? ’ For this reason the Almighty said, responding to their doubt, And how many generations have We destroyed before them? meaning, how many generations have We destroyed? A nation and a generation of deniers whom We destroyed for their disbelief. They were better in furnishings and appearance. That is, they were better than these in wealth, appearances, forms and goods. Al-A’mash said on the authority of Abu Dhibyan on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Better in position and better in company. He said: The position is the home, the company is the assembly, the furniture is the enjoyment, and the company is the view. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “The position is the dwelling, and the company is the assembly, the blessing and the joy in which they were. It is as God said to the people of Pharaoh when He destroyed them and narrated their story in the Qur’an: “How many gardens and springs have they left behind, and crops and noble positions.” So the position is the dwelling and the comfort, and the company is the assembly and the gathering in which they used to gather. God Almighty said in what He narrated to His Messenger about the matter of the people of Lot: And you commit evil in your assemblies. The Arabs call the assembly a club. Qatada said: When they saw the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, in their rough living and among them were scum, the polytheists presented what you hear. Which of the two groups is better in position and better in company? And Mujahid and Al-Dahhak said the same. Some of them said that furniture is money, and some of them said: Some said clothes, and some said furnishings and the view is the view as Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and more than one said, and Al-Hasan Al-Basri said it means pictures, and Malik said the same: furniture and view more money and better pictures, and all are close and correct.

19:75: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who claim that they are right and you are wrong: Whoever is in error, that is, from us and from you, let the Most Merciful extend for him a term, that is, let the Most Merciful give him respite in what he is in until he meets his Lord and his time comes to an end, until, when they see what they are promised, either the punishment, that will befall him, or the Hour, that will come upon him suddenly, then they will know, then, who is worse in position and weaker in soldiers, in response to what they argued about the goodness of the position and the goodness of the host. Mujahid said about His statement: So let the Most Gracious extend for him a term so let God leave him in his transgression, and this is how Abu Ja’far ibn Jarir, may God have mercy on him, decided. This is a challenge to the polytheists who claim that they are on the right path in what they are doing, as God Almighty mentioned the challenge to the Jews in His statement: O you who are Jews, if you claim that you are allies of God to the exclusion of the people, then wish for death, if you should be truthful. That is, claim death for the one who is wrong among us or among you if you claim that you are on the right path, for supplication will not harm you, so they refrained from that, and the report of that has been presented in detail in Surat Al-Baqarah, praise be to God, and as God Almighty mentioned the challenge to the Christians in Surat Al-Imran when they insisted on disbelief and continued in their transgression and exaggeration in their claim that Jesus was the son of God, and God mentioned His arguments and proofs for the servitude of Jesus, and that he was created like Adam, God Almighty said after that: “So whoever disputes with you about him after what has come to you of knowledge, say: Come, let us call our sons and daughters.” And your sons, our women, your women, ourselves, yourselves. Then we supplicate and invoke the curse of God upon the liars.” But they also refrained from doing that.
19:76: When the Almighty mentioned the support of those who are in misguidance in what they are in and their increase in what they are upon, He informed of the increase in guidance of those who are guided, as the Almighty said: And when a surah is revealed, some of them say, ‘Which of you has this increased in faith?’ (Al-Kahf 2:10). And His statement: And the lasting good deeds has been explained and discussed and the hadiths related to them were mentioned in Surat Al-Kahf are better with your Lord as reward meaning recompense and better as outcome meaning consequence and outcome for its doer. Abdul Razzaq said: Umar bin Rashid told us on the authority of Yahya bin Abi Katheer on the authority of Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sat down one day and took a dry stick and crushed its leaves, then he said: ‘Saying La ilaha illa God, Allahu Akbar, Subhan God, and Al-Hamdulillah, erase sins just as the wind crushes the leaves of this tree. Take them, Abu Darda’, before you are prevented from them. They are the lasting good deeds, and they are from the treasures of Paradise.’” Abu Salamah said: When Abu Darda’ mentioned this hadith, he would say: ‘I will declare the unity of God, I will magnify God, and I will glorify God, until when an ignorant person sees me, he will think that I am crazy.’ This appears to be mursal, but it may be from the narration of Abu Salamah on the authority of Abu Darda’, and God knows best. This is how it appears in Sunan Ibn Majah on the authority of Abu Mu’awiyah on the authority of Umar bin Rashid on the authority of Yahya on the authority of Abu Salamah on the authority of Abu Darda’, and he mentioned something similar.
19:77: Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A'mash told us, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Khabbab bin Al-Arat, who said: I was a blacksmith, and Al-'As bin Wa'il owed me a debt, so I went to him to collect it from him, and he said: No, by God, I will not pay you until you disbelieve in Muhammad, so I said: No, by God, I will not disbelieve in Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, until you die and are resurrected. He said: If I die and am resurrected, you will come to Me with wealth and children, and I will give you. Then God revealed: “Have you seen he who disbelieved in Our verses and said, ‘I will surely be given wealth and children?’ Has he known the unseen, or has he taken a covenant from the Most Merciful? No! We will record what he says, and will extend for him a term of punishment. And We will inherit from him what he says, and he will come to Us alone.” It was narrated by the two authors of the Sahih and others from different chains of transmission on the authority of Al-A’mash with it. In the wording of Al-Bukhari: I was a blacksmith in Mecca, and I made a sword for Al-‘As ibn Wa’il, so I came to collect it from him, and he mentioned the hadith and said: Or has he taken a covenant from the Most Merciful? He said: A binding one. Abdul Razzaq said: Al-Thawri told us on the authority of Al-A'mash on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, who said: Khabbab bin Al-Arat said: I was a blacksmith in Mecca, and I used to work for Al-'As bin Wa'il. I had some dirhams owed to him, so I came to collect my debt from him, but he said to me: I will not pay you until you disbelieve in Muhammad. I said: I will not disbelieve in Muhammad until you die and are resurrected. He said: When I am resurrected, I will have wealth and children. I mentioned that to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and God revealed: "Have you seen he who disbelieves in Our verses?" Al-'Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Some men from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, were demanding a debt from Al-'As bin Wa'il As-Sahmi, so they came to him to collect it. He said: Do you not claim that there is gold, silver, silk, and all kinds of fruits in Paradise? They said: Yes. He said: Your appointed time is in the Hereafter, and by God, I will be given wealth and children, and I will be given the same as the book that you brought. So God gave an example of it in the Qur’an, saying: “Have you seen he who disbelieved in Our verses and said, ‘I will be given wealth and children?’ Has he known the unseen, or has he taken a covenant from the Most Merciful? No! We will record what he says, and We will extend for him a period of punishment. And We will inherit from him what he says, and he will come to Us alone.” And this is what Mujahid, Qatadah, and others said: It was revealed about Al-‘As ibn Wa’il. And His statement, I will be given wealth and children, some of them read it with a fat-ha on the waw of childa, and others read it with a damma, and it has the same meaning. Ru’bah said: Praise be to God, the Almighty, the One, who has not taken from any son a son. Al-Harith bin Halza said: I have seen people who have had wealth and children. The poet said: I wish so-and-so was in his mother's womb, and I wish so-and-so was the son of a donkey It was said: The word child with the dammah is plural, and child with the fathah is singular, and it is the language of Qais, and God knows best. He knows the unseen is a denial of this speaker, I will be given wealth and children, meaning on the Day of Resurrection, meaning he knows what he will have in the Hereafter until he swore and took an oath to that, Or has he taken a covenant with the Most Gracious? Or does he have a covenant with God that he will give him that? It was previously mentioned in Al-Bukhari that it is the trustworthy one. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: He knows the unseen or has he taken a covenant with the Most Gracious? He said: There is no god but God, so he hopes for it. Muhammad ibn Ka’b Al-Qurazi said: Except for he who has taken a covenant with the Most Gracious, he said: The testimony that there is no god but God, then he recited: Except for he who has taken a covenant with the Most Gracious. His saying: No is a deterrent letter for what came before it, and an emphasis for what comes after it. We will record what he says meaning his request for that and his judgment of himself as he wishes and his disbelief in God Almighty, and We will extend for him of the punishment a great deal meaning in the Hereafter for his saying that and his disbelief in God in this world, and We will inherit from him what he says meaning of wealth and children, We will take away from him the opposite of what he said, that he will be given in the Hereafter wealth and children in addition to what he had in this world, rather in the Hereafter what he had in this world will be taken away from him, and for this reason God Almighty said: and he will come to Us alone meaning of wealth and children. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and We will inherit from him what he says he said: We will inherit it. Mujahid said: And We shall inherit from him what he says his wealth and his children. This is what Al-Aas bin Wa’il said. Abd Al-Razzaq said on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And We shall inherit from him what he says he said: what he has. And this is His statement: I will be given wealth and children. And in the wording of Ibn Mas’ud: And We shall inherit from him what he has. Qatada said: And he comes to Us alone he has neither wealth nor children. Abd Al-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: And We shall inherit from him what he says he said: what he collected of this world and what he did in it. He said: And he comes to Us alone he said: alone from that, not followed by little or much.

19:81: The Almighty tells us about the disbelievers who associate partners with their Lord, that they have taken gods besides Him so that those gods would be a might that they would take pride in and seek victory from. Then He informed us that the matter is not as they claimed and that what they hoped for will not happen, so He said: No! They will disbelieve in their worship meaning on the Day of Resurrection and will be against them meaning contrary to what they thought about them, as the Almighty said: "And who is more astray than he who calls upon those besides God who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they, of their call, are unaware. * And when the people are gathered together, they will be enemies to them and will be disbelievers in their worship." Abu Nahik read: No! They will disbelieve in their worship. Al-Suddi said: No! They will disbelieve in their worship meaning in the worship of idols. And His statement: And they will be against them means contrary to what was expected of them. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And they will be against them means helpers. Mujahid said: Helpers against them, quarreling with them and lying to them. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And they will be against them means companions. Qatada said: companions in the fire, cursing each other and disbelieving in each other. Al-Suddi said, And they will be against them means fierce opponents in dispute. Ad-Dahhak said, And they will be against them means enemies. Ibn Zayd said: Adversity is affliction, and Ikrimah said: Adversity is regret. And His statement: Have you not seen that We send the devils against the disbelievers, to incite them with [extreme] incitement? Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: to mislead them. Al-Awfi said on his authority: to incite them against Muhammad and his companions. Mujahid said: to disperse them. Qatada said: to disturb them with [an] incitement to the disobedience of God. Sufyan al-Thawri said: to tempt them with temptation and to hasten them with haste. Al-Suddi said: to make them transgress. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: This is like the statement of God the Almighty: And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful - We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion. And His statement: “So be not impatient over them. We are only counting for them a [definite] number.” That is, do not be impatient, O Muhammad, over these people in inflicting the punishment upon them. We are only counting for them a [definite] number. That is, We are only delaying them for a fixed term, and they will inevitably come to the punishment and chastisement of God. He said: And never think that God is unaware of what the wrongdoers do verse, “So give the disbelievers respite. Give them respite for a while.” We only grant them respite that they may increase in sin. “We grant them enjoyment for a little; then We will force them to a severe punishment.” Say, ‘Enjoy yourselves, for your destination is the Fire.’ verse Al-Suddi said: We only count for them a count: years, months, days, and hours. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: We only count for them a count he said: We count their breaths in this world.
19:82: The Almighty tells us about the disbelievers who associate partners with their Lord, that they have taken gods besides Him so that those gods would be a might that they would take pride in and seek victory from. Then He informed us that the matter is not as they claimed and that what they hoped for will not happen, so He said: No! They will disbelieve in their worship meaning on the Day of Resurrection and will be against them meaning contrary to what they thought about them, as the Almighty said: "And who is more astray than he who calls upon those besides God who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they, of their call, are unaware. * And when the people are gathered together, they will be enemies to them and will be disbelievers in their worship." Abu Nahik read: No! They will disbelieve in their worship. Al-Suddi said: No! They will disbelieve in their worship meaning in the worship of idols. And His statement: And they will be against them means contrary to what was expected of them. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And they will be against them means helpers. Mujahid said: Helpers against them, quarreling with them and lying to them. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And they will be against them means companions. Qatada said: companions in the fire, cursing each other and disbelieving in each other. Al-Suddi said, And they will be against them means fierce opponents in dispute. Ad-Dahhak said, And they will be against them means enemies. Ibn Zayd said: Adversity is affliction, and Ikrimah said: Adversity is regret. And His statement: Have you not seen that We send the devils against the disbelievers, to incite them with [extreme] incitement? Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: to mislead them. Al-Awfi said on his authority: to incite them against Muhammad and his companions. Mujahid said: to disperse them. Qatada said: to disturb them with [an] incitement to the disobedience of God. Sufyan al-Thawri said: to tempt them with temptation and to hasten them with haste. Al-Suddi said: to make them transgress. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: This is like the statement of God the Almighty: And whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Most Merciful - We appoint for him a devil, and he is to him a companion. And His statement: “So be not impatient over them. We are only counting for them a [definite] number.” That is, do not be impatient, O Muhammad, over these people in inflicting the punishment upon them. We are only counting for them a [definite] number. That is, We are only delaying them for a fixed term, and they will inevitably come to the punishment and chastisement of God. He said: And never think that God is unaware of what the wrongdoers do verse, “So give the disbelievers respite. Give them respite for a while.” We only grant them respite that they may increase in sin. “We grant them enjoyment for a little; then We will force them to a severe punishment.” Say, ‘Enjoy yourselves, for your destination is the Fire.’ verse Al-Suddi said: We only count for them a count: years, months, days, and hours. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: We only count for them a count he said: We count their breaths in this world.

19:85: The Almighty tells us about His pious friends who feared Him in this world, followed His messengers and believed them in what they told them, obeyed them in what they commanded them to do, and refrained from what they warned them against. He will gather them on the Day of Resurrection as a delegation to Him. A delegation is someone who comes riding, and from this comes the word delegations and their riding on mounts of light from the mounts of the Hereafter. They are coming on the best of missions to the abode of His honor and pleasure. As for the criminals who denied the messengers and opposed them, they will be violently driven to the Fire in a state of thirst, as stated by Ata', Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and more than one. Here it is said: Which of the two groups has a better position and better company? Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj told us, Ibn Khalid told us, on the authority of Amr bin Qais Al-Mala’i, on the authority of Ibn Marzouq, On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation, he said: The believer will be met when he comes out of his grave in the most beautiful image he has ever seen and the most pleasant smelling, and he will say: Who are you? He will say: Do you not know me? He will say: No, except that God has made your smell pleasant and your face beautiful, and He will say: I am your righteous deeds, this is how you were in this world, good deeds and goodness, and I have always ridden you in this world, so come and ride me, and he will ride him, and that is what He said, On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation, and Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, On the Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation, he said: Riders. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Al-Muthanna told me, Ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, The Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation, he said: On camels. Ibn Jurayj said: On fine camels. Ath-Thawri said: On she-camels. Qatada said: The Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation, he said: To Paradise. Abdullah bin Imam Ahmad said in his father’s Musnad: Suwaid bin Saeed told us, Ali bin Masahr told us, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Ishaq, An-Nu’man bin Saad told us, he said: We were sitting with Ali, may God be pleased with him, and he recited this verse: The Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation, he said: No, by God, they will not be gathered on their feet, nor will the delegation be gathered on their feet, but on she-camels the likes of which mankind has never seen, on which are saddles of gold, and they will ride on them until they knock on the gates of Paradise. This is how Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Abd Al-Rahman bin Ishaq Al-Madani. He added to it saddles of gold, its reins of emerald, and the rest was like it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated here a very strange hadith on the authority of Ali, saying: My father told us, Abu Ghassan Malik bin Ismail al-Nahdi told us, Muslima bin Jaafar al-Bajali told us, I heard Abu Muadh al-Basri say: Ali was one day with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he recited this verse: The Day We shall gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation. He said: I do not think that a delegation is anything other than a group, O Messenger of God? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “By Him in whose hand is my soul, when they emerge from their graves, they will be greeted or brought white she-camels with wings and on them are saddles of gold, the straps of their sandals, a light that shines with every step as far as the eye can see. They will come to a tree from whose root two springs will spring. They will drink from one of them, and it will wash away whatever filth is in their bellies. They will wash themselves from the other, and their skin and hair will never be disheveled after that. The freshness of bliss will flow over them. They will come to the gate of Paradise, and there will be a ring of red ruby on sheets of gold. They will strike the ring on the sheet, and a ringing sound will be heard from it, ‘O Ali!’ It will be conveyed to every houri that her husband has come. So her guardian will be sent, and it will be opened for him. When he sees him, he will fall down before him - Muslimah said: I think he said prostrating - and he will say: ‘Raise your head, for I am your guardian and I have been entrusted with your affair.’ So he will follow him and follow in his footsteps. The houri will be overcome by the rush, and she will emerge from the tents of pearls and rubies until…” She embraces him, then says: You are my love and I am your love, I am the immortal who does not die, I am the gentle who does not grieve, I am the satisfied who does not get angry, I am the resident who does not move, then he enters a house from its top to its roof a hundred thousand cubits, its construction is made of pearl stones in different ways: red, yellow, and green, none of which is similar to its companion. And in the house are seventy beds, on each bed seventy mattresses, on each mattress seventy wives, on each wife seventy garments, the marrow of her leg can be seen from behind the garments, he has intercourse with her in the amount of one night of your nights, the rivers beneath them flow rivers of water that is not stagnant, he said: Clear, with no turbidity in it, and rivers of milk whose taste has not changed and has not come from the udders of cattle, and rivers of wine delicious to those who drink it, which men have not squeezed with their feet, and rivers of honey purified, which has not come from the bellies of bees, so he finds the fruits sweet, so if he wishes he may eat standing, or sitting, or reclining, then he recites: And their shades are drawn low over them, and are made easy for them. “Its fruits are tamed.” So he desires food, and a white bird comes to him, or perhaps he said a green one, and it raises its wings and he eats from its sides, whatever color he wants, then it flies away and the angel enters and says: “Peace be upon you. This is the Paradise which you have inherited because of what you used to do.” And if a hair from the hair of the houri were to fall to the people of the earth, the sun would shine with it blackness in light. This is how it appears in this narration, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. We have narrated it in the introductions from the words of Ali, may God be pleased with him, in a similar manner, and it is more likely to be correct, and God knows best. And His statement: And We will drive the criminals to Hell, thirsty, meaning thirsty, they will not possess intercession, meaning they will have no one to intercede for them as the believers intercede for one another, as the Almighty said, informing about them: For us there are no intercessors, nor a close friend. And His statement: Except for he who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful, this is an intermittent exception meaning but for he who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful, which is the testimony that there is no god but God and the fulfillment of its rights. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Except for he who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful, he said: The covenant is the testimony that there is no god but God, and he disavows before God any power and strength, and he hopes only in God, the Almighty and Majestic. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Uthman bin Khalid al-Wasiti told us, Muhammad bin al-Hasan al-Wasiti told us, on the authority of al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Awn bin Abdullah, on the authority of Abu Fakhita, on the authority of al-Aswad bin Yazid, who said: Abdullah, meaning Ibn Mas’ud, recited this verse: Except for those who have made a covenant with the Most Merciful. Then he said: Make a covenant with God, for God will say on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Whoever has a covenant with God, let him stand. They said: O Abu Abd al-Rahman, teach us. He said: Say: O God, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, for I entrust to You in this worldly life not to leave me to my deeds that bring me closer to evil and distance me from good, and I trust only in Your mercy, so make for me a covenant with You that You will fulfill to me on the Day of Resurrection, for You do not fail to fulfill Your promise. Al-Mas’udi said: Zakariya told me, on the authority of al-Qasim bin Abd al-Rahman, Ibn Mas’ud told us, and he used to circle with them, fearful, seeking refuge, seeking forgiveness, fearing and yearning for You. Then he narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of al-Mas’udi in a similar manner.

They will come to a tree from whose root two springs will spring. They will drink from one of them, and it will wash away whatever filth is in their bellies. They will wash themselves from the other, and their skin and hair will never be disheveled after that. The freshness of bliss will flow over them. They will come to the gate of Paradise, and there will be a ring of red ruby on sheets of gold. They will strike the ring on the sheet, and a ringing sound will be heard from it, ‘O Ali!’ It will be conveyed to every houri that her husband has come. So her guardian will be sent, and it will be opened for him. When he sees him, he will fall down before him - Muslimah said: I think he said prostrating - and he will say: ‘Raise your head, for I am your guardian and I have been entrusted with your affair.’ So he will follow him and follow in his footsteps. The houri will be overcome by the rush, and she will emerge from the tents of pearls and rubies until…” She embraces him, then says: You are my love and I am your love, I am the immortal who does not die, I am the gentle who does not grieve, I am the satisfied who does not get angry, I am the resident who does not move, then he enters a house from its top to its roof a hundred thousand cubits, its construction is made of pearl stones in different ways: red, yellow, and green, none of which is similar to its companion. And in the house are seventy beds, on each bed seventy mattresses, on each mattress seventy wives, on each wife seventy garments, the marrow of her leg can be seen from behind the garments, he has intercourse with her in the amount of one night of your nights, the rivers beneath them flow rivers of water that is not stagnant, he said: Clear, with no turbidity in it, and rivers of milk whose taste has not changed and has not come from the udders of cattle, and rivers of wine delicious to those who drink it, which men have not squeezed with their feet, and rivers of honey purified, which has not come from the bellies of bees, so he finds the fruits sweet, so if he wishes he may eat standing, or sitting, or reclining, then he recites: And their shades are drawn low over them, and are made easy for them. “Its fruits are tamed.” So he desires food, and a white bird comes to him, or perhaps he said a green one, and it raises its wings and he eats from its sides, whatever color he wants, then it flies away and the angel enters and says: “Peace be upon you. This is the Paradise which you have inherited because of what you used to do.” And if a hair from the hair of the houri were to fall to the people of the earth, the sun would shine with it blackness in light. This is how it appears in this narration, with a chain of transmission traceable back to the Prophet. We have narrated it in the introductions from the words of Ali, may God be pleased with him, in a similar manner, and it is more likely to be correct, and God knows best. And His statement: And We will drive the criminals to Hell, thirsty, meaning thirsty, they will not possess intercession, meaning they will have no one to intercede for them as the believers intercede for one another, as the Almighty said, informing about them: For us there are no intercessors, nor a close friend. And His statement: Except for he who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful, this is an intermittent exception meaning but for he who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful, which is the testimony that there is no god but God and the fulfillment of its rights. Ali bin Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Except for he who has taken a covenant with the Most Merciful, he said: The covenant is the testimony that there is no god but God, and he disavows before God any power and strength, and he hopes only in God, the Almighty and Majestic. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Uthman bin Khalid al-Wasiti told us, Muhammad bin al-Hasan al-Wasiti told us, on the authority of al-Mas’udi, on the authority of Awn bin Abdullah, on the authority of Abu Fakhita, on the authority of al-Aswad bin Yazid, who said: Abdullah, meaning Ibn Mas’ud, recited this verse: Except for those who have made a covenant with the Most Merciful. Then he said: Make a covenant with God, for God will say on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Whoever has a covenant with God, let him stand. They said: O Abu Abd al-Rahman, teach us. He said: Say: O God, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, for I entrust to You in this worldly life not to leave me to my deeds that bring me closer to evil and distance me from good, and I trust only in Your mercy, so make for me a covenant with You that You will fulfill to me on the Day of Resurrection, for You do not fail to fulfill Your promise. Al-Mas’udi said: Zakariya told me, on the authority of al-Qasim bin Abd al-Rahman, Ibn Mas’ud told us, and he used to circle with them, fearful, seeking refuge, seeking forgiveness, fearing and yearning for You. Then he narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of al-Mas’udi in a similar manner.
19:88: When the Almighty decided in this noble Surah the servitude of Jesus, peace be upon him, and mentioned his creation from Mary without a father, He began to denounce those who claimed that he had a son, the Almighty, the Holy, and the Exalted far above that, so He said: And they say, 'The Most Gracious has taken a son.' You have certainly done meaning in your saying this a thing terrible. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, and Malik said: meaning great. It is said a terrible thing with the hamza broken or opened, and with its extension also in three languages, the most famous of which is the first. And His saying: The heavens almost burst from it and the earth splits open and the mountains collapse in devastation * Because they attribute to the Most Gracious a son meaning that when they hear this statement from the wicked of the children of Adam, they almost do so out of reverence and veneration for the Lord, because they are creatures and established upon His Oneness, and that there is no god but Him, and that He has no partner or peer, and no son or companion, and no equal to Him, but He is the One, the Eternal Refuge. And in everything there is a sign that indicates that He is One. Ibn Jarir said: Ali told me, Abdullah told us, Muawiyah told me on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: The heavens almost burst from it, and the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in ruin, because they attribute to the Most Merciful a son. He said: Indeed, polytheism terrified the heavens, the earth, the mountains, and all of creation except the two heavy ones, and they almost disappeared because of it due to the greatness of God. Just as the good deeds of the polytheist do not benefit with polytheism, so we hope that God will forgive the sins of the monotheists. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Teach your dead to bear witness that there is no god but God, for whoever says it at his death, Paradise is obligatory for him. They said: O Messenger of God, and whoever says it when he is healthy? He said: That is more obligatory and more obligatory.” Then he said, “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, if the heavens and the earths and everything in them and what is between them and what is beneath them were brought and placed on one side of the scale, and the testimony that there is no god but God were placed on the other side, it would outweigh them.” This is how Ibn Jarir narrated it, and the hadith of the card bears witness to it, and God knows best. Ad-Dahhak said: The heavens almost burst from it meaning they crack in fear of God’s greatness. Abdur-Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said: And the earth splits open meaning in anger at Him, and the mountains collapse in ruins. Ibn Abbas said: Destruction. Saeed bin Jubair said: Destruction means that some of them break on top of others in succession. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Suwaid Al-Maqburi told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, Misa’ar told us, on the authority of Awn, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: “A mountain calls another mountain by its name, ‘O so-and-so, did anyone remember God today?’ It says: ‘Yes,’ and is pleased.” Awn said: “It is for good, I hear. So do they hear falsehood and vanity when it is said and do not hear anything else?” Then he recited: The heavens almost burst from it, and the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse in ruins, because they attribute a son to the Most Merciful. Ibn Abi Hatim also said: Al-Mundhir bin Shadhan told us, Huda told us, Aouf told us on the authority of Ghalib bin Ajrad, a man from the people of Ash-Sham told me in the mosque of Mina, he said: It has reached me that when God created the earth and created the trees in it, there was not a tree on earth that the children of Adam would come to except that they would gain some benefit from it - or he said - there was some benefit for them in it, and the earth and the trees remained like that until the wicked ones of the children of Adam spoke that great word, their saying: The Most Merciful has taken a son, so when they spoke it, the earth trembled and the trees quaked. Kaab Al-Ahbar said: The angels became angry and Hell was inflamed when they said what they said. Imam Ahmad said: Abu Muawiyah told us, Al-A’mash told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, on the authority of Abu Musa, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “No one is more patient with the harm he hears than God. He is associated with others and He assigns to Him a son, while He heals them, protects them, and provides for them.” They both included it in the two Sahihs. In another version: They assign to Him a son, while He provides for them and heals them. And His statement: And it is not befitting for the Most Gracious to take a son means that it is not suitable for Him nor is it befitting for Him due to His majesty and greatness, because there is no equal to Him among His creation, because all of creation are His slaves. For this reason He said: “There is none in the heavens and earth but will come to the Most Gracious as a slave. He has already counted them and numbered them precisely” meaning that He knows their number from their creation until the Day of Resurrection, male and female, young and old, and all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone meaning that there is no supporter or protector for Him except God alone, with no partner for Him, so He rules over His creation as He wills, and He is the Just One who does not wrong an atom’s weight, nor does He wrong anyone.

19:96: God Almighty tells us that He plants for His believing servants who do good deeds - which are deeds that please God Almighty because they follow the Muhammadan Sharia - He plants for them in the hearts of His righteous servants love and affection, and this is something that is inevitable and unavoidable, and authentic hadiths have been reported about this from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from more than one source. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Abu Uwanah told us, Suhayl told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When God loves a servant, He calls Gabriel and says: ‘O Gabriel, I love so-and-so, so love him.’ Gabriel loves him. Then He calls out to the people of heaven: ‘God loves so-and-so, so love him.’ The people of heaven love him, and acceptance is placed for him on earth. When God hates a servant, He calls Gabriel and says: ‘O Gabriel, I hate so-and-so, so hate him.’ Gabriel hates him, and then He calls out to the people of heaven: ‘God hates so-and-so, so hate him.’ The people of heaven hate him, and hatred is placed for him on earth.” Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Suhayl, and Ahmad and al-Bukhari narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj from Musa ibn Uqbah from Nafi’, the freed slave of Ibn Umar, from Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, Maymun Abu Muhammad al-Marai told us, Muhammad ibn Abbad al-Makhzumi told us, on the authority of Thawban, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “A servant seeks to please God Almighty, and he continues to do so. Then God Almighty says to Gabriel: ‘So-and-so, My servant, seeks to please Me. Beware, My mercy is upon him.’ Gabriel says: ‘May God’s mercy be upon so-and-so.’ The bearers of the Throne say it, and those around them say it until the inhabitants of the seven heavens say it, then he descends to the earth.” Strange. They did not narrate it from this source. Imam Ahmad said: Aswad bin Aamer told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Saad al-Wasiti, on the authority of Abu Dhubayyah, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Verily, maqah is from God - Sharik said: It is love - and the fame in the heavens. “So when God loves a servant, He says to Gabriel, peace be upon him: I love so-and-so. Gabriel calls out: Your Lord hates so-and-so, so love him - I see Sharik saying: So love descends for him on earth. And when He hates a servant, He says to Gabriel: I hate so-and-so, so hate him. Gabriel calls out: Your Lord hates so-and-so, so hate him - I see Sharik saying: So hatred for him flows on earth.” Strange, and they did not include it. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Dawud al-Hafri told us, Abdul Aziz - meaning Ibn Muhammad - who is al-Darawardi told us, on the authority of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When God loves a servant, He calls Gabriel: ‘I love so-and-so, so love him.’ He calls out in the heavens, then He sends down love for him among the people of the earth. This is the statement of God Almighty: ‘Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them love.’” Narrated by Muslim and al-Tirmidhi, both of them on the authority of Abdullah, on the authority of Qutaybah, on the authority of al-Darawardi with it. Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan sahih. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: The Most Gracious will appoint for them affection, he said: Love. Mujahid said on his authority: The Most Gracious will appoint for them affection, he said: Love among people in this world. Saeed bin Jubair said on his authority: He loves them and makes them beloved, meaning to His believing creation, as Mujahid also said, and Ad-Dahhak and others. Al-Awfi also said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Affection from Muslims in this world, good provision, and a truthful tongue. Qatada said: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Gracious will appoint for them affection, meaning, by God, in the hearts of the people of faith. It was mentioned to us that Harim bin Hayyan used to say: No servant turns to God with his heart except that God turns to the hearts of the believers to him until He bestows upon him their affection and mercy. Qatada said: Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him, used to say: No servant does good or evil except that God, the Almighty, clothes him in the garment of his deeds. Ibn Abi Hatim, may God have mercy on him, said: Ahmad bin Sinan told us, Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, on the authority of al-Rabi’ bin Subaih, on the authority of al-Hasan al-Basri, may God have mercy on him, who said: A man said: By God, I will worship God with a worship that will make me remember Him. So, he would not be seen at the time of prayer except standing and praying. He was the first to enter the mosque and the last to leave, so he did not show reverence. He remained like that for seven months, and he would not pass by a group of people except that they would say: Look at this hypocrite. So he turned to himself and said: I do not see myself remembering anyone except evil. I will make all my work for God Almighty. So he did nothing more than change his intention, and he did not add to the work he was doing. After that, he would pass by a group of people and they would say: May God have mercy on so-and-so now. And al-Hasan recited: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them love. Ibn Jarir narrated that this verse was revealed during the migration of Abd al-Rahman bin Awf, but this is a mistake, because this surah in its entirety is Meccan and nothing of it was revealed after the migration, and the chain of transmission for that is not authentic, and God knows best. And His statement: We have only made it easy meaning the Qur’an in your language meaning O Muhammad, which is the clear, fluent, and perfect Arabic language that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous meaning those who respond to God and believe in His Messenger, and to warn thereby a stubborn people meaning crooked from the truth and inclined towards falsehood. Ibn Abi Nujayj said on the authority of Mujahid, a stubborn people who do not go straight. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Ismail, who is Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Salih, and to warn thereby a stubborn people crooked from the truth. Ad-Dahhak said: Al-Adad means the opponent. Al-Qurazi said: Al-Adad means the liar. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: A stubborn people means deaf. Others said: Deaf are the ears of the hearts. Qatadah said: A stubborn people means Quraysh. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A stubborn people are wicked. Layth Ibn Abi Salim narrated the same on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Zayd said: The most stubborn oppressor. He recited the words of God Almighty: And He is the most stubborn opponent. And His words: And how many generations before them have We destroyed? meaning, of a nation who disbelieved in the signs of God and denied His messengers. Do you perceive anyone of them or hear a sound from them? meaning, do you see anyone of them or hear a sound from them? Ibn Abbas, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd said: It means a sound. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: Do you see an eye or hear a sound? And the sound in the original language is a low voice. The poet said: She was afraid that her friend would come to her aid, and that her friend would be her sickness. The last interpretation of Surah Maryam, praise and thanks be to God, and it will be followed, God willing, by the interpretation of Surah Taha, praise be to God.
