Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan sahih. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his statement: The Most Gracious will appoint for them affection, he said: Love. Mujahid said on his authority: The Most Gracious will appoint for them affection, he said: Love among people in this world. Saeed bin Jubair said on his authority: He loves them and makes them beloved, meaning to His believing creation, as Mujahid also said, and Ad-Dahhak and others. Al-Awfi also said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Affection from Muslims in this world, good provision, and a truthful tongue. Qatada said: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - the Most Gracious will appoint for them affection, meaning, by God, in the hearts of the people of faith. It was mentioned to us that Harim bin Hayyan used to say: No servant turns to God with his heart except that God turns to the hearts of the believers to him until He bestows upon him their affection and mercy. Qatada said: Uthman bin Affan, may God be pleased with him, used to say: No servant does good or evil except that God, the Almighty, clothes him in the garment of his deeds. Ibn Abi Hatim, may God have mercy on him, said: Ahmad bin Sinan told us, Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, on the authority of al-Rabi’ bin Subaih, on the authority of al-Hasan al-Basri, may God have mercy on him, who said: A man said: By God, I will worship God with a worship that will make me remember Him. So, he would not be seen at the time of prayer except standing and praying. He was the first to enter the mosque and the last to leave, so he did not show reverence. He remained like that for seven months, and he would not pass by a group of people except that they would say: Look at this hypocrite. So he turned to himself and said: I do not see myself remembering anyone except evil. I will make all my work for God Almighty. So he did nothing more than change his intention, and he did not add to the work he was doing. After that, he would pass by a group of people and they would say: May God have mercy on so-and-so now. And al-Hasan recited: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them love. Ibn Jarir narrated that this verse was revealed during the migration of Abd al-Rahman bin Awf, but this is a mistake, because this surah in its entirety is Meccan and nothing of it was revealed after the migration, and the chain of transmission for that is not authentic, and God knows best. And His statement: We have only made it easy meaning the Qur’an in your language meaning O Muhammad, which is the clear, fluent, and perfect Arabic language that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous meaning those who respond to God and believe in His Messenger, and to warn thereby a stubborn people meaning crooked from the truth and inclined towards falsehood. Ibn Abi Nujayj said on the authority of Mujahid, a stubborn people who do not go straight. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Ismail, who is Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Salih, and to warn thereby a stubborn people crooked from the truth. Ad-Dahhak said: Al-Adad means the opponent. Al-Qurazi said: Al-Adad means the liar. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: A stubborn people means deaf. Others said: Deaf are the ears of the hearts. Qatadah said: A stubborn people means Quraysh. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A stubborn people are wicked. Layth Ibn Abi Salim narrated the same on the authority of Mujahid. Ibn Zayd said: The most stubborn oppressor. He recited the words of God Almighty: And He is the most stubborn opponent. And His words: And how many generations before them have We destroyed? meaning, of a nation who disbelieved in the signs of God and denied His messengers. Do you perceive anyone of them or hear a sound from them? meaning, do you see anyone of them or hear a sound from them? Ibn Abbas, Abu Al-Aaliyah, Ikrimah, Al-Hasan Al-Basri, Saeed bin Jubayr, Al-Dahhak, and Ibn Zayd said: It means a sound. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: Do you see an eye or hear a sound? And the sound in the original language is a low voice. The poet said: She was afraid that her friend would come to her aid, and that her friend would be her sickness. The last interpretation of Surah Maryam, praise and thanks be to God, and it will be followed, God willing, by the interpretation of Surah Taha, praise be to God.
19:98: God Almighty tells us that He plants for His believing servants who do good deeds - which are deeds that please God Almighty because they follow the Muhammadan Sharia - He plants for them in the hearts of His righteous servants love and affection, and this is something that is inevitable and unavoidable, and authentic hadiths have been reported about this from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from more than one source. Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Abu Uwanah told us, Suhayl told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “When God loves a servant, He calls Gabriel and says: ‘O Gabriel, I love so-and-so, so love him.’ Gabriel loves him. Then He calls out to the people of heaven: ‘God loves so-and-so, so love him.’ The people of heaven love him, and acceptance is placed for him on earth. When God hates a servant, He calls Gabriel and says: ‘O Gabriel, I hate so-and-so, so hate him.’ Gabriel hates him, and then He calls out to the people of heaven: ‘God hates so-and-so, so hate him.’ The people of heaven hate him, and hatred is placed for him on earth.” Muslim narrated it from the hadith of Suhayl, and Ahmad and al-Bukhari narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj from Musa ibn Uqbah from Nafi’, the freed slave of Ibn Umar, from Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similarly. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, Maymun Abu Muhammad al-Marai told us, Muhammad ibn Abbad al-Makhzumi told us, on the authority of Thawban, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “A servant seeks to please God Almighty, and he continues to do so. Then God Almighty says to Gabriel: ‘So-and-so, My servant, seeks to please Me. Beware, My mercy is upon him.’ Gabriel says: ‘May God’s mercy be upon so-and-so.’ The bearers of the Throne say it, and those around them say it until the inhabitants of the seven heavens say it, then he descends to the earth.” Strange. They did not narrate it from this source.
